💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the next EV to plug in at a ski resort might be the one that groomed your trail.
  • Industry observers note that under the agreement, Kässbohrer will connect its customers with ChargePoint for chargers, software, and support with planning, installation, and day-to-day operations.
  • Industry observers note that kässbohrer’s first fully electric groomer, the PistenBully 100 E, uses electric motors to move the machine and spin the tiller that smooths the snow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the next EV to plug in at a ski resort might be the one that groomed your trail. ChargePoint has struck a deal with Kässbohrer, the German company behind PistenBully snow groomers, to bring charging to ski resorts and indoor ski facilities across Europe and North America.

Industry observers note that under the agreement, Kässbohrer will connect its customers with ChargePoint for chargers, software, and support with planning, installation, and day-to-day operations. Resorts can use the same provider for the snow groomers and other vehicles they keep at the maintenance depot, as well as for the EV chargers skiers use while they’re out on the slopes.

Industry observers note that kässbohrer’s first fully electric groomer, the PistenBully 100 E, uses electric motors to move the machine and spin the tiller that smooths the snow. It has a 196 kWh battery and can handle up to three hours of normal grooming on a charge, according to the manufacturer. It can take up to 22 kW on AC or 150 kW on a DC fast charger. It fast charges from zero to 100% in about an hour.

Industry observers note that chargePoint says Kässbohrer accounts for more than half of the snow groomers sold worldwide each year. Resorts can start working with the companies now. Which resorts will install ChargePoint’s chargers first, and how many will go in, are TBC.

Breaking: Microplastics may be more dangerous than we thought. Scientists just discovered why

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1308 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Plastic is used in everything from food packaging and water bottles to children's toys, largely because it is considered chemically stable and unlikely to react with its surroundings.
  • Recent findings suggest that as larger plastic objects fragment into microplastics and even smaller nanoplastics, the amount of exposed surface area increases dramatically.
  • Recent findings suggest that researchers at Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley identified the chemical processes behind this phenomenon in a fresh study published in Nature.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Plastic is used in everything from food packaging and water bottles to children's toys, largely because it is considered chemically stable and unlikely to react with its surroundings. However, upcoming research suggests that this assumption may not hold when plastic breaks down into extremely small particles.

Recent findings suggest that as larger plastic objects fragment into microplastics and even smaller nanoplastics, the amount of exposed surface area increases dramatically. Scientists have now discovered that these newly exposed surfaces can interact with water in unexpected ways, producing reactive molecules that may harm living cells.

Recent findings suggest that researchers at Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley identified the chemical processes behind this phenomenon in a fresh study published in Nature. Their findings challenge the longstanding idea that microplastics are simply passive fragments of material.

"As plastic fragments into smaller and smaller particles, its surface area increases enormously. Then microplastics change the water that surrounds them, generating high-energy, reactive radicals (reactive oxygen species, ROS) that very likely contribute to biological damage that we see in animals and potentially in humans as a result of microplastic exposure," said Wei Min, a Columbia professor of Chemistry and Biomedical Engineering.

Why Microplastics Could Be Dangerous Inside the Human Body.

Recent findings suggest that the discovery raises important questions about what happens when microplastics enter the human body. Blood and cells contain large amounts of water, creating conditions in which these tiny particles could continue participating in chemical reactions.

Rather than remaining inactive after exposure, microplastics may generate reactive oxygen species, often called ROS. These highly reactive molecules can damage biological structures, including components of cells and tissues. The findings offer a possible explanation for some of the harmful effects associated with microplastic exposure, although they do not establish that this process causes specific diseases in humans.

The research builds on earlier work by Min's laboratory that helped reveal just how widespread microscopic plastic contamination has become.

In a recent development, in a widely reported 2024 study, the Columbia researchers developed a laser-based microscopy technique capable of detecting extremely small plastic particles. Using this technology, they found an average of approximately 240,000 detectable plastic fragments in a single liter of bottled water (mostly nanometer-sized plastic, nanoplastics). That was 10 to 100 times more particles than previous estimates had suggested.

The discovery helped draw greater attention to the presence of microplastics and nanoplastics throughout the food system.

Growing Concerns About Microplastics and Human Health.

Since that earlier research attracted widespread attention, the potential health consequences of microplastic exposure have become an increasingly important public health matter.

In a recent development, in 2026, the federal government launched a $144 million initiative focused on addressing toxic microplastics in the human body. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency also added microplastics to a federal list of contaminants that may be of concern in drinking water, marking their first appearance on the list.

Meanwhile, studies published in major scientific journals, including the Upcoming England Journal of Medicine, Nature Medicine, and Nature Health, have reported associations between exposure to microplastics and nanoplastics and serious conditions such as heart attacks, strokes, dementia, and brain tumors.

However, an important question has remained unanswered. If plastic is generally considered chemically inert, how might these microscopic fragments contribute to biological damage?

The new findings identify a previously overlooked chemical pathway that could help researchers understand these potential health risks.

"Our research found that when microplastics interact with water, as they do when they're in bottled water, or when they're absorbed into our bloodstream, they spontaneously generate what we call reactive oxygen species (ROS)," noted Naixin Qian, a postdoctoral researcher in Wei Min's lab who helped lead the research. "ROS are textbook examples of the kinds of molecules that can damage animal and human tissue.".

How Water Triggers Harmful Chemical Reactions.

One of the most surprising aspects of the discovery is that water plays an active role in the reaction.

It has been revealed that many plastics are hydrophobic, meaning their surfaces repel water. When water encounters these surfaces, the molecules and electrically charged particles near the boundary can behave differently than they do in ordinary water.

It has been revealed that the researchers found that these interactions can encourage electrons to move between chemical species, allowing highly reactive radicals to form. As plastic fragments become smaller, their greater surface area provides more locations where these reactions can occur.

"Water is a key active player here, rather than just a spectator. It's integral to making these microplastics reactive. Water molecules become chemically active when they come into contact with plastic, which is hydrophobic. Contact between the water and plastic creates an environment that facilitates electron transfer, and the formation of reactive radicals. When plastics fragment into smaller particles, their increasing surface-to-volume ratio creates more of these chemically active areas," Min stated.

In a recent development, to investigate the process, the Columbia researchers performed chemical and biological experiments. Their collaborators in Professor Teresa Head-Gordon's laboratory at UC Berkeley used theoretical calculations and computer simulations to examine the interactions between plastic surfaces and water at the molecular level.

It has been revealed that the Berkeley team developed a theoretical explanation showing how hydroxide ions, which are negatively charged particles, can become concentrated in the layers of water immediately surrounding a water-repelling plastic surface. In this environment, the ions can more readily lose electrons and form hydroxyl radicals.

Hydroxyl radicals are particularly reactive chemical species capable of damaging biological molecules. Their formation provides a possible link between the physical breakdown of plastics and the biological effects researchers have observed.

Could the Discovery Lead to Safer Plastics?

Understanding the chemistry involved could eventually help scientists develop plastics that are less likely to generate harmful reactive molecules when exposed to water.

"Our fundamental work that the most hydrophobic microplastics interacting with water can drive chemical reactivity could ultimately lead to new engineering solutions by redesigning the chemistry of these commodity plastics to reduce the toxic outcomes on health and the environment," mentioned Head-Gordon.

Sources indicate that the implications also extend beyond human health. Microplastics can enter rivers, lakes, and other waterways through industrial waste, wastewater, and everyday activities. The newly identified chemical reactions could influence aquatic organisms and ecosystems exposed to these particles.

Co-author Beizhan Yan of Columbia University's Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory emphasized that microplastics can originate from numerous sources, including plastic manufacturing facilities and laundromats. Everyday processes, such as heating materials in a microwave or leaving bottled water exposed to sunlight during storage, can also contribute to the formation of tiny plastic particles.

"This work has significant implications for environmental and human health," remarked co-author Beizhan Yan of Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory. "In certain environments, such as discharges from plastic manufacturers and laundromats, microplastics can form and enter aquatic environments. This work also indicates that radicals can form on hydrophobic plastic surfaces in water, which could affect ecosystems and human health following exposure. In addition, various uses and processes in our daily lives can generate microplastics, including microwave heating, sunlight exposure of bottled water during storage. This foundational work provides a potential pathway for understanding their health impacts.".

By revealing that microplastics can actively alter the chemistry of surrounding water, the research adds a upcoming dimension to concerns about plastic pollution. It also establishes a potential mechanism for investigating how these widespread particles interact with living systems, while opening the door to strategies for reducing their environmental and health risks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Get ready to return to Pharloom as the previously revealed Hollow Knight: Silksong DLC might be closer than you imagined. Team Cherry has just announced a new presentation stream named Cherry Time!, where they’re promising to give us new info on the previously announced expansion for their latest game.

Hollow Knight: Silksong lived up to its hype when it was first released back in 2025, and just like its predecessor, it didn’t take long until a newly introduced enhancement was announced. However, in a very Silksong fashion, we barely had any new info on it, aside from its name and a promise to be “coming soon”.

This is the first time we’ll be getting an actual patch on this expansion, which has only received a single teaser trailer so far. And the Silksong announcement might not be the only thing we’ll be seeing here.

Industry observers note that throughout its social media accounts, Team Cherry has declared their Cherry Time! Livestream, a newly introduced presentation they haven’t done before. You can watch it live on November 27, 7 AM PT on their official YouTube channel.

Team Cherry is promising “a bunch of exciting announcements” aside from the already expected info on Sea of Sorrow, the Silksong DLC. This could be either new updates for the game, unrelated to the DLC, or even new titles from one of the world’s most secluded dev teams.

Aside from the initial trailer released back in 2025, the team has been radio silent about its development. This might actually be a great sign, as you’ll know if you’ve followed anything about Silksong’s development cycle in the past years.

It has been revealed that the game was originally conceived as an expansion for the original Hollow Knight, where you could play as the supporting character Hornet. However, the project became too significant for its own good, eventually turning into a whole fresh game in just a few years.

This could be either fresh updates for the game, unrelated to the DLC, or even new titles from one of the world’s most secluded dev teams.

According to recent reports, however, Team Cherry was adamant about never feeding us any fresh info, leading fans to think the game was quietly canceled or that it was all a hoax from the start. You’ll certainly remember those frenzied fans typing “SKONG??!!” on every single indie game announcement stream (or any stream, really). Things got out of control at a time.

Imagine the shock when we discovered Team Cherry was just too busy adding fresh things to the game over the years and had adopted a chronically offline posture. We only got actual info less than a month before the game actually came out. We might be seeing history repeating itself here, but I wouldn’t count on it just yet.

While we were promised that the waiting wouldn’t be as daunting as it was for the base game (which took 8 years to release after the first title), it seems like Sea of Sorrow might be going through the same development hell cycle.

The recently released physical edition of Silksong for the Nintendo Switch presented the upcoming DLC as a “giant expansion” and made no latest notes to the 2026 release window, as shown by Reddit user ArchivistOfSkylands.

For all we know, Team Cherry might be taking their time cooking another huge meal for us once again. It certainly won’t take 8 more years again, but we might not be visiting this upcoming ocean of content this year just yet.

In a recent development, the original Hollow Knight had a total of four free updates, which added tons of content such as fresh endings, more quests, new bosses, and many boss gauntlets to prove yourself as a real God in Hallownest. Fans have huge expectations for Silksong to get the same treatment, especially when it comes to the latter.

In a recent development, we’ll know more about the current state of this expansion in just a few more days. We got a release date for Silksong similarly, coming almost out of nowhere, so it might be the time. But as we’ve seen lately, devs have been taking extra time to refine their final game, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see that happen here, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stellantis is preparing its exit from the World Endurance Championship (WEC) and Formula E, but the automaker isn’t giving up on motorsports. In fact, the decision is meant to funnel more energy into making motorsports-focused cars for customers.

In a recent development, the Peugeot 9X8 hypercar is Stellantis’s only factory-backed car in the WEC; that partnership will end at the end of the year. The automaker has a bit more skin in the game in Formula E, where Citroën and Opel each hold two spots on the 24-car grid this season. Both teams will exit Formula E at the end of the season in summer 2027.

Recent findings suggest that by ending its FIA World Championship partnerships, Stellantis claims it’ll be able to focus on building motorsports-capable cars for enthusiasts. Employees who currently work in the WEC and Formula E divisions will be retained and reassigned to other areas focused on performance-vehicle development and customer racing. Those reassigned employees will likely pivot to work on high-performance Alfa Romeo and Maserati models, as well as newly introduced motorsports-inspired variants for Peugeot, Lancia, and Opel.

According to recent reports, stellantis claims it’ll continue to build on its engineering and competition knowledge in customer racing programs—especially rally racing, where several of its brands have deep rally roots. Dismantling factory-backed teams likely frees up the automaker to invest more in smaller collaborations with privateer teams, much like its partnership with PH Sport on the Lancia Corse HF in the World Rally Championship.

Recent findings suggest that the restructuring aligns with Stellantis’s FaSTLAne 2030 strategy, which aims to launch more than 100 upcoming and refreshed vehicles by 2030. Reassigning motorsports employees to other areas will undoubtedly help streamline the development process for enthusiast-focused cars to meet the automaker’s ambitious goals.

In a recent development, car and Driver reached out to Stellantis to find out how this might affect its involvement in other major motorsports events in North America. After all, Ram recently returned to the NASCAR Truck Series for the 2026 season, and Dodge recently confirmed aims to return to the NASCAR Cup Series for the 2027 season with two Charger-based race cars. A spokesperson provided the following statement: “There are no changes to Stellantis North America motorsports programs.”.

NASA's powerful Moon rocket engine roars through a dramatic 200-second test

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA has successfully completed another powerful rocket engine test as the agency prepares for future Artemis missions that will return astronauts to the Moon and lay the groundwork for human exploration of Mars.
  • On November 18, engineers fired RS-25 engine No.
  • According to recent reports, although this particular engine is not intended for spaceflight, the successful test will provide NASA and its primary contractor, L3Harris Technologies, with valuable performance data.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA has successfully completed another powerful rocket engine test as the agency prepares for future Artemis missions that will return astronauts to the Moon and lay the groundwork for human exploration of Mars.

On November 18, engineers fired RS-25 engine No. 10001 at the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA's Stennis Space Center, located near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. The developmental engine ran for its full scheduled duration of three minutes and 20 seconds (200 seconds).

According to recent reports, although this particular engine is not intended for spaceflight, the successful test will provide NASA and its primary contractor, L3Harris Technologies, with valuable performance data. Engineers will use the results to improve the power, efficiency, and reliability of RS-25 engines designed for upcoming Artemis missions.

Powerful RS-25 Engines Will Help Send Astronauts Back to the Moon.

NASA is preparing for Artemis IV, a mission scheduled for 2028 that aims to land astronauts on the lunar surface. The mission will launch from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, using the massive Space Launch System (SLS) rocket to carry astronauts aboard the Orion spacecraft.

Artemis IV represents an important step toward NASA's larger ambitions. The agency intends to explore the Moon's South Pole, establish a sustained human presence on the lunar surface, and develop the experience and technologies needed for the first crewed journey to Mars.

The RS-25 engines play a crucial role in making these missions possible. Each SLS rocket uses four of the engines, which together generate up to 2 million pounds of thrust to help propel the spacecraft off the launchpad and into space.

Before any RS-25 engine is cleared for flight, it must undergo testing at NASA's Stennis Space Center to verify that it can perform reliably under the extreme conditions of a rocket launch.

These tests are carried out by specialists from NASA, L3Harris Technologies, and Nova Space Solutions, working together to ensure the engines are ready to power future journeys beyond Earth.

If I could only use one bike lock, it’d be this: FoldyLock Elite 110 review

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1518 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that I ride e-bikes professionally, regularly testing new bikes and biking gear.
  • Of course, the name of the game in bike theft prevention is to use more than just one lock, and I’m going to return to that idea at the end of this article.
  • But for now, believe me when I say that this lock is seriously good, to the point that it has become my newly introduced primary.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I ride e-bikes professionally, regularly testing new bikes and biking gear. I don’t even own a car – I get around almost exclusively on two wheels. So when it comes to vital gear like bike locks for my fleet of e-bikes, I’ve become pretty well-versed out of necessity. And after testing out the world’s strongest folding lock, the FoldyLock Elite 110, I’m more than impressed. If I could only have one lock for my e-bikes, it’d be this one.

Of course, the name of the game in bike theft prevention is to use more than just one lock, and I’m going to return to that idea at the end of this article.

But for now, believe me when I say that this lock is seriously good, to the point that it has become my newly introduced primary.

The FoldyLock Elite 110cm is identical in strength and security to the FoldyLock Forever 90cm that I tested a few years ago, yet is 20 cm (8 inches) longer, reaching 110 cm (43 inches).

According to recent reports, the FoldyLock Forever 90 and FoldyLock Elite 110 are the strongest folding locks in the world, confirmed by the premier international lock certification organization ART. These are the only folding locks that have ever achieved a 3-star ART certification. The scale goes up to 5, but 4-star and 5-star certifications are motorcycle-level locks.

To make things even more impressive, the FoldyLock line achieved that ART 3-star rating three years ago, and no other lock company has matched it on a folding lock since.

If one independent and international lock testing association isn’t enough for you, the lock is also Sold Secure GOLD rated, which is just one step below Sold Secure’s highest ever rating for bike locks.

Again, more on that at the end of this article to get you to that last step for top security.

There are a lot of different styles of locks out there, and each has its own advantages and disadvantages. But as someone who rides e-bikes every day as his job, I’ve come to the opinion that a strong folding lock has the best combination of maximizing advantages and minimizing disadvantages.

For starters, folding locks allow you to lock to larger diameter anchors that would be impossible for U-locks (trees, telephone poles, multiple fence bars, etc). They’re more compact than chain locks of comparable security, both in size and weight. They’re significantly stronger than cable locks (when made with quality materials). And they mount more easily to a bike frame than nearly any other lock style, as they fold tightly and usually come with a holster.

Recent findings suggest that yes, there are disadvantages too. The segments mean they can’t form as close to a circle as a chain, meaning the maximum size of the tree or telephone pole you’re locking to is slightly smaller than for an equal length chain. And they usually aren’t quite as strong as U-Locks made with angle-grinder-resistant materials. But for their size and convenience, they make perhaps the best single style of lock for the best pairing of strength and convenience.

According to recent reports, since I began testing the FoldyLock Elite 110, I’ve been living with it as my main e-bike lock. I test a lot of locks, and most go onto the shelf when I’m done as backups or to give to friends/family. But the FoldyLock Elite 110 has stayed as my newly introduced primary lock, and here’s why.

First of all, as I mentioned, it’s the strongest folding lock in the world, as confirmed by multiple independent testing organizations. So if you want the advantages of a folding lock, there’s simply none more secure than this.

But beyond that, the FoldyLock Elite 110 is covered by multiple patents, including the specialized protected rivets that prevent nut splitter attacks and that take out any squeaks or rattles that are common in other folding locks. The lock also physically locks into its holster, which keeps it both secure (no bounce-outs) and helps keep it silent during the ride. There’s even a coating on the hardened steel segments to protect my bike frame from scratches and resist corrosion during winter use (plus a shutter on the locking mechanism for additional winter corrosion resistance).

Basically, it seems like the organization has taken pretty much all of the learnings from previous locks in their lineup, and applied those lessons to the FoldyLock Elite, making it a perfect combination of strength, security, and convenience.

As I mentioned, after my time testing the FoldyLock Elite, I can say for sure that if I could only use one bike lock, it would be this one.

But I don’t just use one bike lock. And I recommend you don’t either, if you can swing it.

Sources indicate that we’ve long known that the best way to keep your bike safe from thieves is to use two bike locks. It’s partly for the extra security, and partly for the extra time it takes a thief to work on defeating two locks, meaning they’re more likely to choose a different sucker’s bike to steal.

It has been revealed that I always recommend using two different styles of bike locks. Think: folding lock plus U-lock, or U-lock plus chain lock, or chain lock plus cable lock, or cable lock plus folding lock, etc. You get the idea.

My FoldyLock Elite is now my primary lock, and it allows me to lock onto just about everything on the street, from official bike racks to chunky utility poles. For my secondary, I use a SeatyLock Mason 220. This U-lock is actually one step higher-rated by Sold Secure, reaching that testing organization’s Diamond level – its highest level of security rating.

In a recent development, when I can lock both the folding lock and U-lock to an anchor, I do it. But sometimes, when I’m forced to lock to something wide like a lamppost, I lock the frame and rear wheel with the FoldyLock Elite 110, then lock the front wheel to the frame with the Mason 220 U-lock, as seen in the photo above.

Industry observers note that that keeps both of my wheels and my bike locked. Despite there only being one lock keeping the bike in place to the anchor (lamppost), the second lock adds an extra layer of frustration for a thief and is likely to convince them to just choose the next bike on the sidewalk.

Industry observers note that that’s why I always recommend using two different locks, and ideally of different styles. I believe the FoldyLock Elite 110 offers the most advantages, but its few disadvantages are offset by a secondary lock, such as a strong U-lock.

When it comes to mounting, I’ve got the holster mounted onto my fork using the supplied flexible mounting straps.

Normally you’d mount it to one of your bottle mounts, but I only have a single set of bottle bosses on my e-bike’s frame, and they are currently taken up by a water bottle holder (surprise!).

I found that despite adding 1.9 kg or 4.1 lb to the side of my fork, my bike still rides just fine. The advantage of a rigid frame is that there’s not really much change to the unsprung mass since everything is unsprung!

I love riding hands-free in the city, and it did take me a day or two to get used to the slightly altered steering moment, but I can still ride my bike hands-free even with the extra weight there on the side of the fork.

At some point I might shift the holster onto the rear rack or swap it out for my bottle holder in favor of a newly introduced bottle spot, but so far it’s working great there and hasn’t caused me any handling problems.

In a recent development, when it comes to value, I think the FoldyLock Elite 110 takes the cake here, too. It’s normally priced at an MSRP of $145, though it’s right now on sale for $119 as part of the Black Friday promotions.

As I noted, I test hundreds of bikes and dozens of locks as my day job. I live and breathe bikes. The fact that this lock has become my go-to everyday lock is pretty much all you need to know about how impressive it truly is. It’s a pleasure to live with and use, which means that I actually end up using it.

A Used Cybertruck Is Selling A Month Faster Than A Ford F-150

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (661 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you had to guess which used pickup found a buyer fastest in October, the Toyota Tacoma would be a sensible bet.
  • In a recent development, the data from the new iSeeCars study covers 1.1 million used vehicles that changed hands in October, so this was before Tesla declared it would discontinue the Cybertruck in 2027.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Cybertruck surpassed all other pickups, averaging 39.1 days, compared to 65.5 days for used pickups overall.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you had to guess which used pickup found a buyer fastest in October, the Toyota Tacoma would be a sensible bet. It’s America’s best-selling midsize truck and has a reputation for holding its value. Or you might pick the super frugal Ford Maverick Hybrid. But the truck that beat them both was the Tesla Cybertruck.

In a recent development, the data from the new iSeeCars study covers 1.1 million used vehicles that changed hands in October, so this was before Tesla declared it would discontinue the Cybertruck in 2027. The study looked at one- to five-year-old vehicles and ranked models by how long they’d been listed before selling.

Recent findings suggest that the Cybertruck surpassed all other pickups, averaging 39.1 days, compared to 65.5 days for used pickups overall. The Maverick Hybrid came closest at 43.3 days, followed by the Rivian R1T at 45.2 and the F-150 Lightning at 47.4. The Tacoma came in fifth position.

The gap between the two electric pickups at either end of the list was even more striking. A used Chevrolet Silverado EV took 107.5 days to sell, putting it last among the 24 trucks in the study. That’s a 68-day difference between two American electric pickups. Across the wider used market, EVs averaged about 46 days to find a buyer, around nine fewer than hybrids and 15 fewer than gas vehicles.

According to recent reports, how swiftly a used Cybertruck sold seems to have changed a lot since May 2024, when some sellers were cutting as much as $30,000 from their asking prices after listing their trucks for close to $200,000. By December of that year, we reported that used Cybertrucks were piling up on dealer lots, with data at the time showing they stayed for 75 days, up from 27 in May.

Then owners got a look at what Tesla itself would pay for a used Cybertruck trade-in. One year later, in May 2025, one owner of a $99,990 dual-motor Foundation Series truck got a trade-in estimate of $65,400 after driving it just 6,211 miles.

So even though the Cybertruck was the fastest-selling used pickup in iSeeCars’ newly introduced study, it didn’t report what buyers paid, so we don’t know whether owners got their asking price or had to lower it to sell.

According to recent reports, tesla will build the last Cybertrucks at the end of summer 2027, and this will reshape their used market. Elon Musk originally confirmed production would end around the middle of the year, but then extended the run to fill more orders. And if you order a Cybertruck now, the only one you can get is the $110,000 tri-motor Cyberbeast, so anyone who wants a less expensive dual-motor truck has to look for a used example.

Once the last new Cybertruck is sold, I’d expect collectors and everyday truck buyers to look at used ones differently. Someone after a clean Foundation Series truck with low miles might pay a little extra for one close to home, especially since it could be months before another comes up for sale nearby.

At the same time, someone who just needs an electric pickup to tow a trailer has more options. If a used dual-motor Cybertruck costs about the same as a Ford F-150 Lightning or a Rivian R1T, I suspect that buyer will care more about mileage, condition, and how much battery warranty is left than when Tesla built its last truck.

Latest Update: Battlefield Labs is coming back for a short session to test out next week's Battlefield 6 update, and you can expect more tests in the future, too

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season enhancement not intended to change the game significantly.
  • However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.
  • Sources indicate that the December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the new year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season enhancement not intended to change the game significantly.

However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

Sources indicate that the December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the new year. We’ve known about its content for a while, and it’s definitely the lightest, compared to the two previous phases.

In a recent development, battlefield Studios revealed a host of new changes that will be included in the same patch, which are apparently significant enough to require player testing. The developer is reviving Battlefield Labs to help it do so, but only for three two-hour sessions, split across the game’s three main server regions (EU, NA, APAC).

All tests are scheduled for today, December 2, and they remain under NDA. Battlefield Labs is also sticking with PC as its chosen platform yet again, though you will be able to join through Steam this time, alongside the EA app.

It has been revealed that the focus of the test will be on three key areas that the December 9 patch will be touching. First, there’s footstep audio, an problem that was really brought into focus with the launch of Redsec Battle Royale. You can expect to hear enemy footsteps from farther away, and intuitively know the type of surface they’re moving on.

The patch also brings another pass to hit registration and netcode, which BF Studios says should improve responsiveness in close-quarter situations. Finally, there are broader changes to other combat areas that the announcement didn’t elaborate on.

All testing will take place on Eastwood, and Operation Firestorm, rotating between Conquest, and Escalation.

Industry observers note that going forward, Battlefield Studios said to expect Labs to be open to more players, and for the process itself to be smoother. The developer wants to have faster turnaround times, after all, so that the initiative can test smaller changes and be more responsive to player feedback.

Industry observers note that some of the more involved, future sessions will include experiments with map layout changes and various other non-standard compositions of player and vehicle numbers. Of course, you can also expect upcoming maps and modes to be tested in Labs, similar to how the CTE was used in Battlefield 4’s long life.

Comparison Test: Audi SQ5 vs. BMW X3 vs. Genesis GV70 vs. Mercedes-AMG GLC

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3129 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • From the November/December 2026 glitch of Car and Driver.
  • The vehicles assembled here are not the starring members of their makers’ lineups.
  • Industry observers note that we could have made a wider casting call for this production, but to ensure that the chosen crossovers weren’t forgettable, we opted for the more muscular variants, the ones with a more potent optional engine.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From the November/December 2026 glitch of Car and Driver.

The vehicles assembled here are not the starring members of their makers’ lineups. They aren’t built for lapping racetracks, crossing the Rubicon Trail, or carrying a crew of seven. Instead, compact luxury crossover SUVs, as their compound-modifier designation suggests, play multiple roles. As premium-brand offerings, there’s an expectation of luxury. As four-door utilities, they must accommodate passengers and cargo. And as the more sporting examples of their ilk, they should exhibit a degree of athleticism. Living at the intersection of a variety of vehicle types, they need to demonstrate versatility and range, rather than excel with a singular ability.

Industry observers note that we could have made a wider casting call for this production, but to ensure that the chosen crossovers weren’t forgettable, we opted for the more muscular variants, the ones with a more potent optional engine. That dramatically narrowed the field of candidates.

See all results for new 2026 Audi SQ5 for sale near 59701.

The Audi Q5 is a relatively fresh face, having just been redesigned for the 2025 model year. The SQ5 is the model that fit our bill, with its 362-hp turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6, seven-speed dual-clutch automatic, and sport-tuned adaptive air-spring suspension. The Prestige package ($5900) and Black Optic package ($1900) were the chief items pushing this crossover’s $66,795 base price to $76,370.

Recent findings suggest that the BMW X3 is a seasoned player in this arena, and the M50 xDrive best met our criteria. The turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six has bulked up and boasts 393 horsepower and a robust 428 pound-feet of torque. It’s paired with an eight-speed automatic, adaptive M suspension, M Sport brakes, and an M Sport rear differential. To the BMW’s $67,850 base price, our test example added a modest load of options, which included the Premium package ($2750) and the M Sport Professional package ($600). The result was the lowest as-tested price, at $72,050.

Where you find a BMW, you typically find a Mercedes. Here, that’s the GLC in its upcoming-for-2027 AMG GLC53 guise. It brings an enhanced supercharged and turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six that makes 443 horsepower, a nine-speed automatic, AMG Ride Control suspension with adaptive damping, and rear-axle steering. Its $71,350 base price soared to $85,920, inflated by extras that included the Pinnacle trim ($3900), the AMG Dynamic Plus package ($2000), and the Driver Assistance package ($1950).

The award-winning Genesis GV70, with multiple 10Best trophies on its mantel, was a natural to include. It arrives in 3.5T guise, powered by a 375-hp twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V-6 paired with an eight-speed automatic. It surprised us by having the highest base price, at $72,045, but in Prestige Graphite trim, there was little more to add, resulting in an as-tested figure of $73,895.

See all results for fresh 2026 Audi SQ5 for sale near 59701.

What about the many other hopefuls from Alfa Romeo, Cadillac, Lexus, Lincoln, Land Rover, and Volvo? Most were screened out due to insufficient horsepower below our 350-pony threshold, while dedicated hybrids and electrics were not invited. Casting is a cruel process.

In a recent development, let’s face it; none of this quartet have movie-star looks. The GV70, though most familiar (the design dates from 2022), is still pleasing to our eyes. The GLC’s appearance doesn’t break much newly introduced ground, but its long hood and rakishly set-back greenhouse give it an aristocratic vibe. The Audi’s fresh sheetmetal somehow seems not so fresh, and also not so interesting; it was the hardest of the four to pick out in traffic. Then there’s the BMW. Like a celebrity who experiments with creative facial hair or a weird ’do, BMW periodically feels the need to challenge its fans by changing up its look. Unfortunately, that’s where the X3’s design now finds itself.

HIGHS: Comfortable seats, capable chassis, solid feature content. LOWS: Forgettable looks, cramped rear quarters, not really a standout anywhere. VERDICT: Plenty of ability but eschews the spotlight.

That change-for-change’s-sake mantra reaches full flower in the X3’s interior. The operation of the outboard air vents and the placement of their controls are just annoying, as are the haptic door-lock buttons. “What the hell is going on with the door panels?” asked associate news editor Jack Fitzgerald. The design aims to be more futuristic than luxurious, but BMW’s vision of tomorrow is somewhat dystopian. “There’s nothing I like about these design choices,” noted managing testing editor David Beard, “not one thing.” Screens and lighting set the scene, the better to distract you from the cheap-looking materials. After dark, though, the offending bits recede, and the glowing mood lighting enhances the atmosphere. Space is not an problem. The back seat comfortably accommodates two, but the shape of the seatback makes it uncomfortable for three (although that’s probably a rare use case for this segment). Up front, some of us found the driver’s seat to be narrow, but it’s highly effective at holding you in place during cornering.

Sources indicate that look at the SQ5’s dash, and it’s more like an assemblage of screens than a coherent design—the tacked-on passenger’s display is part of the Prestige package. Our car’s red seats and suede door panels were enlivening elements, but the patterned black plastic trim would look downmarket even in an A3. The driver’s chair was deemed good for a variety of body types, and the adjustable-height center armrest ups the comfort quotient. The SQ5 was also one of two vehicles in this test with seat massagers (the Genesis was the other). Its back seat, though, was the hardest to access and the least comfortable once you fold yourself into place—a consequence of the SQ5’s shortest-in-test wheelbase.

The GLC53’s cabin looks richer than its German compatriots’, and this is one Mercedes model whose significant screen isn’t larger than life. Whereas BMW tries pointlessly to reinvent the air vent, Mercedes reveals what a quality execution looks like. This AMG steering wheel still has annoying touch-swipe pads, though. We also noticed that the bloated center console impinges on the driver’s kneeroom, and the inductive charging pad buried deep within made the Mercedes the car in which you’re most likely to leave your phone (it will warn you that you’ve left it inside). Finally, the GLC’s set-back cabin results in a smaller cargo hold than others here.

HIGHS: Lowest as-tested price, best fuel economy, just misses first place in most measures of performance. LOWS: Odd-duck appearance, off-putting interior, not so richly equipped. VERDICT: An SUV that dares you to like it.

The GV70’s interior is the most glam, even more so than the Mercedes’s. “Easily the nicest,” Beard said. “You notice it from the moment you sit down.” Partial credit goes to the nonboring color scheme—blue with splashes of bright red—but don’t discount the glossy carbon-fiber-weave trim, the bright stainless-steel finishes, the ovoid shapes, and the quality-feeling switchgear. We love the rotary controller for the infotainment, which feels like quality. Unfortunately, it also feels like, and is located just ahead of, the rotary shifter. That quibble aside, the user-friendly GV70 took top marks in ergonomics. The Genesis also boasts comfortable, though firm, front chairs, with bonus points for their extendable under-thigh support.

Recent findings suggest that if it’s an action hero you’re seeking, look first to the Mercedes. It has the strongest résumé, with not just the most horsepower but also the most torque, at 443 pound-feet (472 with a 10-second overboost function), just shading the BMW. Though tasked with carrying the greatest mass (4669 pounds), the boosted inline-six shrugs that off, and the AMG races to 60 mph in a launch-controlled 3.7 seconds, or in 4.7 seconds from a rolling 5-mph street start. Both of these results are best in test. So, too, are the quarter-mile time of 12.2 seconds at 113 mph and, thanks to the optional AMG Dynamic Plus package, the top speed of 167 mph, should you have to outrun a hail of bullets from machine-gun-wielding bad guys. All of this was plenty evident from behind the wheel, where the Mercedes felt like it wanted to storm the autobahn.

The BMW, with its “fantastic powertrain” (Beard again), was just a beat behind. Commendably boasting the lowest curb weight of 4474 pounds, the X3 posted a 60-mph time of 4.0 seconds flat, with a street-start figure of 4.9 seconds, both second best among our foursome, as was its quarter-mile time. Exhaling through quad exhaust outlets, and piping the exhaust note through the audio system, the vocal straight-six sounds great when giving its all. “The grunt is always right there,” noted Buyer’s Guide associate editor Andrew Wendler, but if you somehow don’t trust the highly responsive transmission to deliver—or you just want a more theatrical experience—you can pull and hold the downshift paddle to trigger a 10-second Sport Boost mode. It puts the powertrain into its max-sport settings, although it had no measurable effect at the test track. It does call up a cool 10-second countdown graphic in the instrument cluster. “It reminded me of the Power Rangers activating,” Wendler noted.

The Audi also has a potent powertrain that’s always ready to break into a run, although it doesn’t sound quite as good as the others when doing so. “The 90-degree V-6 doesn’t have much character,” opined Beard. Nevertheless, with 406 pound-feet of torque, the SQ5 scampers to 60 mph in 4.3 seconds, or 5.2 seconds from a rolling start. Its seven-speed was the only dual-clutch automatic here and had the expected snappy responses but almost none of the low-speed lurching behavior commonly found in such transmissions.

HIGHS: Bucks-up cabin that’s a pleasure to interact with, blissful ride, quiet cruising.LOWS: Slowest of the group, trails on the skidpad, eyebrow-raising base price.VERDICT: Not the hardest-charging but still undeniably endearing.

Recent findings suggest that with the second-smallest stable of ponies at 375, along with a lowest-in-test 391 pound-feet of torque, the Genesis had noticeably less vigor than the Germans. That bore out at the track, where the GV70’s 60-mph time of 5.1 seconds was 0.8 second behind its nearest rival. The GV70 tied the Audi in 30-to-50-mph passing but otherwise brought up the rear in all acceleration tests. Still, the Genesis is hardly slow, and the V-6 makes the right noises when the virtual tach needle climbs. For the most part, fuel economy represents a bit part for these players, but the BMW’s 28 mpg in our hands bested the rest of the group and shaded the second-place Audi by 4 mpg. Meanwhile, the Genesis racked up the biggest bar tab, quaffing premium at a rate of 21 mpg.

Industry observers note that asked to show their softer side, the Mercedes and the BMW struggle. They remain firm even in the mellowest suspension modes, and any leftover compliance goes away if you switch into Sport. Of the BMW, Fitzgerald noted, “The suspension really beats you up on this loop, especially in Sport.” The X3 suffered noticeable head toss on the more challenging secondary roads.

Driven over rumble strips or expansion joints, the SQ5 seemed a shade less solid than the others. We posited that it was the lightest car here; actually, the Audi is second to the BMW but only by 16 pounds.

HIGHS: Pavement-searing acceleration, faithful steering, loads of stick. LOWS: Stiff ride, tiresome road noise, budget-busting price. VERDICT: A hugely talented but sometimes annoying A-lister.

None of the Germans rode as well as the Genesis, which barely acknowledged broken pavement. Wendler praised it as “serene on the highway.” Furthering that impression, the GV70 was also the quietest by far, registering just 19 sones at 70 mph.

On the handling loop, the flip side for the GV70 was a bit more body lean in aggressive cornering, though that’s a trade-off many owners would be happy to make. Shod with Michelin Primacy Tour A/S tires, the GV70 didn’t have the grip of the other cars. It also turned in the longest stopping distance, although its firm pedal feel won plaudits, as did the SQ5’s.

Recent findings suggest that the Audi hangs on in the corners—like the Mercedes, it wears Michelin Pilot Sport 4 SUV tires—but the steering doesn’t have much to say. We didn’t love the BMW’s steering either, but its handling chops are substantial even if its Pirelli P Zero All Season footwear placed it third in skid-pad grip with 0.85 g (a previous X3 M50 wearing Goodyear Eagle F1 summer rubber did 0.90 g). With four-wheel steering, the GLC53 turns in eagerly, and we also liked the distinct on-center accuracy. Furthermore, it turned in the best skid-pad numbers and shortest stopping distance.

Coolly capable though it may be, the BMW was hard to warm up to. It hit a lot of marks, and not just at the test track. Its potent powertrain also had the best fuel economy. The Bimmer had the lowest as-tested price, but the least money bought the least equipment, and no one was a fan of the interior—the design, the materials, or interacting with it.

In a recent development, the Audi had no glaring weaknesses—unless you were trying to climb into the back seat—but no scene-stealing moments either. The powertrain and the chassis are undeniably accomplished, but the SQ5 would shine brighter if Audi could recapture some of its design magic, both inside and out.

Sources indicate that in this high-strung company, the Genesis was decidedly not the sportiest, but it should be sporty enough for most drivers. It’s easily the most comfortable, arguably the most luxurious, and just so pleasant to interact with. That was enough for second best overall, despite a last-place finish in most performance metrics.

Sources indicate that the Mercedes ultimately stole the show after acing our track tests. The GLC53 was engaging and exciting. “This is a machine doing powerful stuff, and you’re part of it,” Wendler said. While we admired the SUV’s abilities, it was not free of irritants, with road noise, ride quality, and some ergonomic foibles trying our patience. Sharp-eyed accountants might also point out that the as-tested price was much higher than the others, but some $5K of that was costume jewelry such as black leather with red stitching, 21-inch AMG cross-spoke wheels, and the AMG Night package. All of those options could easily be shed without dimming the GLC53’s star power. And then there’s this truism: Great talent rarely comes cheap.

Tech Report: Take-Two's GTA 6 PC Port Crackdown Has Already Taken Down Over 3,000 Repositories

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (555 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that leonida was named after the fictional state in which GTA 6 takes place, and it was one of several attempts to get the console version running on a computer.
  • It has been revealed that the developers had asked customers to supply their own game files, but Take-Two argues that the project was designed specifically to make use of the leaked build.
  • GitHub indicates it acted on the entire network of 3,007 repositories.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that leonida was named after the fictional state in which GTA 6 takes place, and it was one of several attempts to get the console version running on a computer. Unlike some of the fan-made PC ports we've seen for older console games, though, this one was being developed using a build of a game that had only just come out.

It has been revealed that the developers had asked customers to supply their own game files, but Take-Two argues that the project was designed specifically to make use of the leaked build. The company requested that GitHub take down Leonida and its forks, arguing that the alleged infringement couldn't be addressed without disabling the repositories altogether.

GitHub indicates it acted on the entire network of 3,007 repositories. That number includes forks, which are essentially copies of a repository that other GitHub consumers can work on independently. That doesn't mean there were 3,007 different GTA 6 PC ports in development, though.

An Xbox Series build of GTA 6 was leaked on November 20, with the Leonida repository appearing a day later.

Recent findings suggest that according to PC Gamer, the team appeared to have reached the game's splash screen during a livestream before it crashed. The project's lead developer, NotRexed, subsequently unveiled their departure, citing the loss of the Discord server as well as the pressure of managing the community alongside school and sports.

Take-Two's takedown hasn't put an end to Leonida, either. According to the same report, others have already tried to pick up where the original developer left off.

It's a familiar situation for those of us who primarily play on PC. GTA 4 came to PC several months after its console debut, while we had to wait more than a year and a half after GTA 5's original launch for its PC version. Even Red Dead Redemption 2 took roughly a year to make its way over.

The difference this time is that a report has suggested GTA 6 could arrive on PC in the first quarter of 2027. If that turns out to be true, the wait would be much shorter than it was for Rockstar's last two major releases. There hasn't been an official announcement confirming that release window, however.

Getting GTA 6 to boot on a PC and getting it to run well enough to play through the entire game are two very different things. Just look at how badly Rockstar handled GTA 4's PC port. Even hardware that far exceeded the game's original system requirements struggled to run it smoothly, and Rockstar never bothered to properly fix it.

Modders have spent years ironing out its performance complications and bugs, and while that's still an ongoing process, I'd argue 2026 has been the best year yet to play GTA 4 on PC. Even if one of these unofficial efforts eventually makes it past the splash screen, there's no telling how well the game will run on a typical gaming PC or whether it'll have major bugs throughout the story.

Sources indicate that hopefully, Rockstar won't keep us in the dark for too long regarding the official PC version. Even an approximate release window would be welcome at this point, especially for anyone holding off on buying a console just to play GTA 6.

Alzheimer’s breakthrough exposes a hidden flaw in the brain’s cleanup system

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1372 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A gene that helps the brain contain harmful protein buildup may play a crucial role in Alzheimer's disease.
  • The research, led by John Lukens, PhD, focused on a gene called CASS4, which previous studies had repeatedly linked to an increased risk of Alzheimer's.
  • "These findings break upcoming ground in our understanding of how this genetic risk factor contributes to Alzheimer's disease," stated Lukens, director of UVA's Harrison Family Translational Research Center in Alzheimer's and Neurodegenerative Diseases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A gene that helps the brain contain harmful protein buildup may play a crucial role in Alzheimer's disease. Researchers at UVA Health have discovered that when this gene stops functioning properly, the brain's natural defenses become less effective, allowing toxic plaques to accumulate more rapidly. The findings could point toward new ways to detect, treat, or potentially prevent the disease.

The research, led by John Lukens, PhD, focused on a gene called CASS4, which previous studies had repeatedly linked to an increased risk of Alzheimer's. Until now, however, scientists knew little about what the gene actually does. The team discovered that CASS4 helps regulate microglia, specialized immune cells that act as the brain's cleanup and defense system. When the gene's activity was disrupted, these cells struggled to respond to harmful plaques. They also became much less effective at containing and compacting the toxic material, allowing the plaques to expand and spread more aggressively.

"These findings break upcoming ground in our understanding of how this genetic risk factor contributes to Alzheimer's disease," stated Lukens, director of UVA's Harrison Family Translational Research Center in Alzheimer's and Neurodegenerative Diseases. "Our work further suggests that defective CASS4 activity may serve as an early-onset biomarker to detect Alzheimer's and that therapeutic strategies which boost its function may offer a much-needed approach to treat this devastating brain disease.".

How the Brain's Cleanup System Protects Against Alzheimer's.

Recent findings suggest that more than 6 million Americans are living with Alzheimer's, a progressive disease that gradually damages memory and thinking abilities. As the condition advances, people can lose the ability to recognize even their closest family members, including their own children. Alzheimer's is the sixth-leading cause of death in the United States, according to the figures cited by the researchers.

Sources indicate that two major changes in the brain are associated with the disease. One is the accumulation of amyloid-beta plaques, sticky deposits of protein that collect between nerve cells. The other is the formation of twisted tangles of a protein called tau. Both are hallmarks of Alzheimer's, but growing evidence suggests that the brain's immune system, particularly its microglia, also plays an vital role in how the disease develops.

Microglia normally help protect the brain by responding to threats and managing harmful material. When amyloid-beta plaques appear, these immune cells can surround them with protective barriers and compress the deposits into smaller, more tightly packed structures. This containment process helps limit the damage the plaques can cause to surrounding brain tissue.

The UVA researchers found that CASS4 is vital for maintaining this protective response. When the gene was disrupted in laboratory mice, microglia became less capable of controlling amyloid-beta plaques. As a result, the plaques accumulated more rapidly, nearby nerve cells called neurons suffered damage, and the animals experienced worsening cognitive function.

A Little-Known Alzheimer's Gene Reveals Its Role.

Recent findings suggest that "Despite CASS4 being an Alzheimer's risk gene, really nothing is known about what this gene does or how it affects the brain during disease. Our lab sought to address this major knowledge gap with this paper," said Addie Walsh, UVA physiology graduate student and first author of the paper. "These are notable findings because they give us upcoming insight into how this understudied AD risk gene functions in the brain and suggest that CASS4 may normally help microglia respond to amyloid pathology.".

The researchers also discovered that losing CASS4 set off a series of changes in the activity of other genes. These widespread effects could have implications beyond Alzheimer's, potentially helping explain biological processes involved in other neurodegenerative diseases, which progressively damage nerve cells.

One of the most significant findings was where CASS4 appears to exert its influence. Scientists had previously suspected that the gene contributed to Alzheimer's primarily through its effects on neurons, the cells responsible for transmitting information throughout the brain. Instead, the new research indicates that its main role is in the immune system.

According to recent reports, that distinction could be vital for developing future treatments. Rather than focusing exclusively on neurons or the proteins that accumulate in Alzheimer's, researchers may be able to strengthen the immune cells that help protect the brain from those deposits. The UVA team believes that increasing CASS4 activity or improving microglial function could eventually offer ways to slow or prevent the disease.

A Potential Fresh Target for Alzheimer's Treatments.

"We are now actively exploring potential roles for CASS4 in multiple other neurodegenerative disorders and developing novel strategies to therapeutically target it," said Lukens, of the Department of Neuroscience at the University of Virginia School of Medicine. "Many in the field initially presumed that CASS4 was likely functioning in neurons to influence Alzheimer's. Our findings shift this paradigm by proving that CASS4 predominantly acts through the immune system. This is particularly exciting, as it has only been in recent years that immune-targeting strategies have been considered for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, and this remains an untapped therapeutic avenue with tremendous potential.".

The findings suggest that the brain's immune defenses may offer an important opportunity for future Alzheimer's therapies. They also raise the possibility that defective CASS4 activity could eventually serve as an early warning sign of the disease, potentially helping doctors identify people at risk before more serious symptoms develop.

However, these possibilities remain to be tested. The experiments showing increased plaque buildup, neuronal damage, and cognitive decline were conducted in mice. Further research will be needed to determine whether targeting CASS4 can produce similar protective effects in humans.

According to recent reports, the work is part of a broader effort at UVA to translate laboratory discoveries into treatments for serious diseases. Lukens leads the Harrison Family Translational Research Center in Alzheimer's and Neurodegenerative Diseases, which operates within UVA's newly established Paul and Diane Manning Institute of Biotechnology. The institute was created to accelerate the development of medicines and other therapies for complex medical conditions using advances from UVA's biomedical research programs.

Lukens is also a member of UVA's Center for Brain Immunology and Glia (BIG Center), which studies the roles of immune cells and other supporting cells in brain health and disease.

Walsh, meanwhile, is preparing to continue her research into the brain's immune system in a new position.

In a recent development, "I will be heading to Boston at the end of the year to start my postdoctoral research with the Neurodegeneration Team at the pharmaceutical manufacturer Novartis," she noted. "I am looking forward to continuing to study microglia in neurodegeneration.".

Alzheimer's Gene Discovery Published in Scientific Journal.

The research was published in the Journal of Experimental Medicine. The authors are Adeline E. Walsh, Benjamin A. Davis, Joshua D. Samuels, William A. Mills III, Jessica M. Thanos, Alexis M. Johnson, Katelyn A. Moore, Michael A. Puchalski, Eric J. Steacy, Benjamin W. Wendell, Amélie Daugherty-Lopès, Adrian A. Shimpi, Ukpong B. Eyo and Lukens. The researchers reported having no financial interest in the work.

Among the contributors is Davis, a fourth-year biology student at UVA, who says participating in scientific research has helped shape his approach to problem-solving and his plans for a career in medicine.

In a recent development, "I think that undergraduate research develops a kind of critical thinking that is difficult to cultivate inside a classroom," he mentioned. "My experience with research has taught me to approach questions systematically and never assume there will be a clear answer. As I prepare to apply to medical school, I know these experiences will shape how I approach clinical care and the broader field of science.".

It has been revealed that funding came from the National Institutes of Health's National Institute on Aging through grants R01AG071996, R01AG087406, RF1AG078684 and R01AG086344. Additional support was provided by the Cure Alzheimer's Fund, the Owens Family Foundation, the Harrison Family Foundation, the Rick Sharp Foundation, and the Steven A. Newman AD Award.

Materials provided by University of Virginia Health System. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

You can also save $150 on the Vorsa, which is an awesome all-around e-bike with multiple levels for riders who want higher or lower performance.

Sources indicate that last but not least, the Prodigy V2 Eco is just $1,295 after the $100 deal, which is literally the most affordable Bosch-powered electric bike in the world. The only thing stopping me from buying that bike is that I already have one, though at this price, part of me wonders if I should get a spare for friends to use!

Basically, Ride1Up has a ton of Black Friday Sales going on now, and you can check them all out here.

If you want to go a bit further up the quality ladder to get a more premium e-bike, but you still don’t want to spend $2k+, then you should check out Monarc Bikes. It was founded by Lectric eBikes as an offshoot that could focus on building higher-end models while still leveraging Lectric’s industry heavyweight status to get better pricing. That means the manufacturer can offer higher-end e-bikes that rival some of the bike shop brands, while still offering direct-to-consumer pricing, 5-year warranties, and industry-leading local customer support by phone and email.

The two models they’ve launched so far are the urban-focused Tracer and the off-road-optimized Marker, though you better believe they’ve got more interesting stuff coming, likely next year. For now, though, these two models cover most folks’ needs and come with higher-end parts like quad-piston hydraulic disc brakes, reverse arch forks, Bafang’s powerful motors, large batteries, and impressive add-ons like rear-facing radar to keep tabs on approaching cars.

The tech giant started by selling e-bikes that came with a free spare battery, but has recently opened up options for single or even no-battery bikes, meaning if you previously bought a Monarc model and already have that free spare battery, you can save a bunch of money by buying only the bike and using your spare battery across the line. Yep, it’s like the power drill model!

You can see all of the sales and deals here!

According to recent reports, jackRabbit may be a bit of a divisive brand due to how different the bikes look, but I freakin’ love these things! My JackRabbit OG is one of my prized possessions, and I just love how much performance and convenience JackRabbit has been able to pack into small-format two-wheelers that start at barely 25 lb (11 kg).

Industry observers note that literally every one of their micro e-bikes is 20% off, meaning you’re saving hundreds of dollars. But then the rest of their gear is up to 50% off, such as 30% off their massive RangeBuster batteries.

Check out all of the sales here.

The awesomeness of JackRabbit’s Micro-bikes is a micro-hill I’m prepared to die on, and I definitely recommend these models to anyone who wants a compact electric two-wheeler that rides as stable as a typical Class 2 e-bike but can fold flat to fit in a tiny space like behind a couch or under a dorm room bed.

I’m never parting with my own JackRabbit, and I love seeing new riders discover just how much fun these awesomely strange bikes are!

Austin, Texas-based Mod Bikes doesn’t get as much press as some of the larger players, but I think they deserve a second look for several reasons. Not only are they continuously pushing out fresh and impressive bikes as well as cool technology alongside them (don’t forget about their locking streetside charging stands for e-bikes!), but they also have cool rides that no one else has managed to create.

It has been revealed that case in point: The Mod Easy Sidecar e-bike that looks like a million bucks, but costs just $3,495 after the $400 deal for Black Friday. I love this e-bike for riding around with my nephews as well as the family dog, which you can see below.

There’s even a Sahara version of it that looks like it just got back from an incredible desert expedition!

Industry observers note that juiced Bikes was revived this year, and the firm is back with a vengeance! The high-performance bikes are better than ever, and the prices are better, too!

Industry observers note that the recently introduced Scrambler Mini leads the pack in pricing, starting at just $949 thanks to its Black Friday promotional price. That’d be an awesome model for any young riders this season. But the larger versions are also pushing the value war forward with their own great sales.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a lot to like here, from higher-end parts to 5-year warranties to the backing of the nation’s largest e-bike company, Lectric eBikes. Basically, it’s hard to imagine finding a better deal on a moto-style electric bike these days than from Juiced.

Sure, e-bikes are my first love, but electric scooters absolutely deserve their place in the micromobility ecosystem thanks to their extreme portability and compact, space-saving size.

VMAX is my favorite electric scooter organization, which brings its Swiss design to the US and European scooter markets. When it came to putting my nephew on a scooter to get to school, I made sure he had a VMAX VX2 Lite to cruise around safely and securely. That scooter is marked down to just $639 for Black Friday, despite offering impressive performance of 25 mph (40 km/h) and over 50 miles (80 km) of range! I reviewed that scooter recently and can tell you that the price is more than worth it!

The fresh VX4 is a 37 mph (60 km/h) model that is on sale for just $1,199, though you can get the previous version of that scooter with slightly more muted performance for an even better price of $889!

There are a lot of great deals to be had, and you can see all of VMAX’s sales here.

These are the major sales that jumped out at me, but let me know what other sales you’ve seen on e-bikes you recommend.

I’ll take a look too and update if I see something I know I can stand behind. There are a lot of great e-bikes out there, and having ridden so many by now, I love being able to share my experiences, especially when there’s a good deal to be had at the end!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that hoYoverse just hosted a sizeable Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, revealing more than just the game’s next major enhancement. Version 3.8 was the massive highlight, of course, with the new release arriving soon, on December 16-17 depending on your server region.

Recent findings suggest that alongside showing everything coming with this next update, the developer also announced that 3.8 will go on for eight weeks, rather than the usual six. V3.8 is dubbed "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams", and it brings an end to the Amphoreus journey.

The story in "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams" takes place after the final battle of Amphoreus, where Constance "The Dahlia" appears to deliver a twist: the Trailblazer's memories are scattered, with many parts missing.

According to recent reports, this final quest revolves around finding them in order to piece together the mystery, and involves a return to Penacony. This memory-hunting adventure is told from the perspective of Firefly, which will also explain how she entered the dreamscape initially and met the squad.

In a recent development, the upcoming playable character is The Dahlia, whose power is linked to the the Remembrance path, which allows her to fabricate memories. Despite taking her powers from the Remembrance, The Dhalia actually follows the Path of Nihility in-game: she’s a 5-Star character who shines in teams dealing Break DMG.

Sources indicate that the Dhalia can unleash a Gloomy Zone that causes Toughness Reduction inflicted by allies to trigger Super Break DMG, even before you break your enemies’ Weaknesses. The Dahlia can also invite one teammate to become her Dance Partner, which allows them (and her) to deal additional Super Break DMG each time they attack an enemy. If you trigger her Ultimate after picking a Dance Partner, she applies Type Weaknesses of both partners to enemies.

While The Dahlia is the only new character appearing in this final Amphoreus enhancement, there'll be reruns aplenty, with an unusual third banner phase to make up for the extra long wait for 4.0. Appropriately for her role in the story, Firefly will make her return alongside The Dahlia in Phase 1, while Fugue and Lingsha will both have banner reruns in Phase 2, which is expected on January 7th. A bonus two-week-long Phase 3 will then begin on January 28th, seeing brief reappearances for popular returning characters Aglaea and Sunday, before things (presumably) go back to normal with the new annual update.

Something else to look forward to in 3.8 is The Chrysos Awoo Championship, which invites players to become chimera trainers and compete in team-based battles. The Remnants of Twilight event kicks off with the upcoming patch, too, featuring its own set of challenges. However, HoYoverse have confirmed that there won't be an extra event during Phase 3 — but hopefully that'll give you some time to wrap up the last of the Amphoreus story content, which is longer than the previous four chapters put together.

#144997. Industry News: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
