⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that unlike ordinary body fat, brown fat burns calories to generate heat, making it an attractive target for future obesity treatments.
  • While white fat primarily serves as an energy reserve, brown adipose tissue uses energy to keep the body warm.
  • Exposure to cold naturally activates brown fat, prompting scientists to search for medications that could mimic this response.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that unlike ordinary body fat, brown fat burns calories to generate heat, making it an attractive target for future obesity treatments. Researchers at the University of Basel and University Hospital Basel have now investigated whether medication can switch on this energy-burning tissue in humans. Their surprising findings suggest that harnessing brown fat with drugs may be more challenging than anticipated.

While white fat primarily serves as an energy reserve, brown adipose tissue uses energy to keep the body warm. People with more active brown fat also tend to be leaner and have better metabolic health.

Exposure to cold naturally activates brown fat, prompting scientists to search for medications that could mimic this response. A research team led by Professor Matthias Betz at the University of Basel and University Hospital Basel examined whether activating a specific receptor, known as the beta2 adrenergic receptor, could stimulate brown fat in humans. Their findings were published in the journal Cell Metabolism.

Drug Boosts Calorie Burning Without Clear Brown Fat Activation.

In a recent development, to investigate, the researchers conducted two experiments involving 11 healthy volunteers. They compared the effects of mild cold exposure with those of fenoterol, a medication that stimulates beta2 adrenergic receptors. The scientists measured how much energy the participants expended and used PET/CT scans to monitor brown fat activity.

Both interventions caused the body to burn more energy. However, the scans revealed an important difference. Only cold exposure produced clear evidence of brown fat activation, with the tissue absorbing considerably more glucose than it did following fenoterol administration.

"We were surprised that energy expenditure increased strongly with fenoterol even though we could not detect a comparable activation of brown fat," says Betz. "Our study indicates that an increase in energy expenditure does not automatically mean that brown fat has been activated.".

Exactly where the additional energy is being consumed remains a mystery. The researchers suspect that fenoterol may increase energy consumption in other tissues, potentially including skeletal muscle or white fat.

Implications for Future Weight Loss Drugs.

According to recent reports, the findings also suggest that the biological mechanisms controlling brown fat in humans are more complex than previously thought. Analysis of human tissue indicates that fully activating brown fat may require the combined action of multiple receptors or biological signals rather than stimulating a single receptor.

According to recent reports, understanding these mechanisms could open new possibilities for treating obesity. Current weight loss medications work by reducing appetite. However, as people shed pounds, their bodies often compensate by burning fewer calories.

A treatment that simultaneously reduces appetite and increases calorie burning could help counteract this metabolic adaptation.

"Ideally, we could combine a reduction in appetite with an increase in energy expenditure," says Betz. "But first we need a better understanding of how brown adipose tissue is regulated.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

Sources indicate that the BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

In a recent development, kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

It has been revealed that 90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the manufacturer contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two quickly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Grand Theft Auto VI is a game where you spend a lot of time behind the wheel. Always has been. But sometimes, you just won't feel like actively driving, but you also don't to waste money on a cab.

Recent findings suggest that this is where Auto Drive comes in. It lets the game take over and drive you where you need to go in real time and all with a cinematic camera that shifts and moves, letting you take in the environment without all that pesky "having to pay attention to the road." Red Dead Redemption 2 had the same feature, and I have fond memories of taking advantage of it to watch Arthur ride his horse through that game's incredible environment. It's a great option in GTAVI, but how to use it and turn it on isn't immediately apparent.

In a recent development, first, you must select a destination. Get the GPS set up to direct you to where you want to go.

According to recent reports, next, start driving. The Auto Drive is smart, but doesn't seem to be smart enough to make three-point turns or back out of parking lots. You need to be on your way before you can turn it on.

Once you're on the path, hold down in the d-pad and press start to activate Cinematic.

Once you've done this you should be able to hold down the Circle button on PlayStation or the B button on Xbox to activate Auto Drive and... voilà! You can sit back and let Jason or Lucia take the wheel. They will drive legally, even stopping at lights, but you can speed them up if they're taking too long.

I've always enjoyed driving in Grand Theft Auto, but I was grateful to find this almost-hidden option early in the game.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Upgrade 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios declared it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

Sources indicate that the patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

Sources indicate that the end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

According to recent reports, the other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

According to recent reports, finally, the enhancement makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

World’s largest trial of robotic knee replacement reveals surprising results

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1270 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that robotic technology can help surgeons perform knee replacement operations with greater precision, but that accuracy does not necessarily translate into better results for patients.
  • Robotic technology is becoming increasingly common in knee replacement surgery around the world.
  • Sources indicate that the UK-wide RACER-Knee trial was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) in partnership with Stryker, the manufacturer of the robotic equipment evaluated in the study.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that robotic technology can help surgeons perform knee replacement operations with greater precision, but that accuracy does not necessarily translate into better results for patients. The RACER-Knee trial, the world's largest clinical study of its kind, found that patients who underwent robot-assisted knee replacement experienced similar levels of pain, mobility, and recovery to those who received conventional surgery. The findings provide important evidence about the use of robotics in health care and highlight where future technological developments and research could make a difference. Coordinated by the University of Warwick and University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire (UHCW) NHS Trust, the trial was published in The Lancet, the world's oldest and one of its best-known general medical journals.

Robotic technology is becoming increasingly common in knee replacement surgery around the world. It is now used in 6% of procedures in the UK, 16% in the US, and 42% in Australia. The technology is designed to help surgeons position artificial knee joints more accurately and customize procedures to suit each patient's anatomy.

Sources indicate that the UK-wide RACER-Knee trial was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) in partnership with Stryker, the manufacturer of the robotic equipment evaluated in the study. The Warwick Clinical Trials Unit, UHCW NHS Trust, and the Royal Orthopaedic Hospital in Birmingham led the research. It represents the world's largest double-blinded, randomized controlled trial comparing traditional total knee replacement with procedures performed using the Stryker Mako robotic system, the most widely used system of its kind worldwide.

Greater Precision Does Not Improve Recovery.

Industry observers note that twelve months after surgery, patients in both groups reported comparable recovery, mobility, and pain levels. Although the robotic system enabled surgeons to operate with greater precision, patients did not experience measurable improvements in their overall outcomes during the first year. The researchers also found no increased risk of serious adverse events associated with robotic assistance, suggesting that it was as safe as conventional surgery.

The trial was jointly led by two chief investigators in the UK.

Industry observers note that professor Andrew Metcalfe, of Warwick Medical School at the University of Warwick and a consultant orthopedic surgeon at UHCW NHS Trust, stated: "We are delighted to have completed this world-leading randomized trial of an exciting technology that is now being used globally and at scale. It is an crucial step in the process of innovation and will stimulate lots more high-quality studies. We are very grateful for the support of the many patients who took part which is so important, but also the NIHR and Stryker for working so well together to support this critical study. Technology such as this could really help the care we give for patients, but for robotic-assisted knee replacements, there is still work to do before we see benefits such as less pain or better movement.".

It has been revealed that professor Edward Davis, a consultant orthopedic surgeon at The Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Foundation Trust and honorary professor at the University of Birmingham, remarked: "The trial demonstrates robotic-arm-assistance allows for higher precision, and in theory the system should allow surgeons to customize the procedure according to a patient's anatomy. These results are by no means a condemnation of the robotic systems, but more understanding of the ideal position for a knee replacement and personalization for each patient is needed. We'll then be able to truly take advantage of the advanced precision of robotic systems.".

According to recent reports, professor Anthony Gordon, director of the NIHR Health Technology Assessment (HTA) Programme, stated: "Innovation in healthcare depends on evaluating promising technologies rigorously and at scale. While this study demonstrates robotic-assisted knee replacement is not yet improving patient outcomes, it highlights opportunities to refine these technologies and harness their precision to deliver better care in the future. The NIHR continues to fund robust studies, such as RACER, ensuring we learn how to deliver the latest technologies most effectively within the NHS.".

How Robotic Knee Replacement Works.

Industry observers note that total knee replacement is among the most frequently performed elective surgical procedures worldwide for people with knee arthritis. During traditional surgery, orthopedic surgeons use standard surgical instruments and rely on their training and experience to position the artificial joint.

Robotic technology offers an alternative approach in which the surgeon controls a robotic arm during the operation. The system helps position surgical instruments with exceptional accuracy and allows surgeons to adjust the angles and depths of their cuts with greater flexibility. These capabilities make it possible to customize procedures to individual anatomy in ways that are not achievable with conventional techniques.

Landmark Trial Finds Similar Patient Outcomes.

The study involved 339 patients treated by 33 surgeons at 10 hospitals across the UK. Despite the potential advantages of robotic technology, researchers found no meaningful difference between the two groups in the trial's primary outcome measure, the Forgotten Joint Score, one year after surgery.

This assessment measures how conscious patients are of their artificial joint while carrying out everyday activities. Ideally, a successful knee replacement allows patients to go about their daily lives without frequently noticing the artificial joint. Patients achieved similar scores regardless of which surgical technique was used.

Other measures also indicated comparable results. These included walking ability, pain during hospitalization, pain during the first three months of recovery and at 12 months, and the likelihood of requiring another operation.

Researchers initiative to monitor participants for ten years to determine whether differences between the two surgical approaches emerge over a longer period. One particularly crucial question is whether robotic assistance reduces the number of patients who eventually need additional knee surgery.

Robotic Knee Surgery Takes Longer and Costs More.

Operations performed with robotic assistance required additional time (on average 10.5 minutes) and cost approximately £950 more per procedure.

Although the robotic system improved surgical precision, it was not associated with a higher risk of serious adverse events, indicating that the procedure appeared to be as safe as traditional knee replacement.

However, when assessed against current NHS spending thresholds, the robotic technology evaluated in the trial was not considered cost-effective during the first year following surgery.

The Future of Personalized Knee Replacement.

The researchers believe that robotic technology could become more valuable if surgeons learn how to use its enhanced precision to better accommodate differences in individual patients' anatomy.

Industry observers note that determining the ideal placement of an artificial knee joint for each patient could eventually allow surgeons to turn greater technical accuracy into meaningful improvements in recovery, pain relief, and mobility. Achieving those benefits will require further technological development and additional research, making personalized robotic surgery a promising area for future investigation.

The findings of the RACER-Knee trial were published in The Lancet.

The research was organized by University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust and the University of Warwick. Funding was provided by the UK NHS research organization, the National Institute for Health Research, through its Health Technology Assessment Programme (NIHR128768).

Recent findings suggest that stryker, the manufacturer that manufactures the robotic system, covered the additional expenses associated with performing robotic surgery during the trial. The company did not participate in analyzing or interpreting the study results.

You'll need to find the sweet spot with the left stick and hit R2 on PlayStation or RT on Xbox to pick the door, which adds a whole new layer to robberies.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales.
  • All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they declared a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.

All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they declared a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

In a recent development, the lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation". In a press release, they say they've filed suit on behalf of anybody who bought Intel stock from July 23rd to October 29th this year.

The suit claims that Intel neglected to tell investors that falling PC and component sales were having a "materially greater negative impact" on their third financial quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Groupresults than Intel had previously stated – to the tune of "hundreds of millions of dollars" in revenue shrinkage, compared to the previous quarter, with the situation still expected to "worsen".

They also accuse the firm of keeping schtum about the aforesaid "massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", together with the fact that "any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup described above.".

Finally, they say Intel bosses have failed to disclose that they're struggling to procure an adequate supply of substrates – that is, materials used to create the base layer of chips, circuit boards and similar components. As such, the lawyers claim, Intel couldn't "ramp up production to meet data center CPU demand even if the Firm chose to divert production resources because of a slowdown in PC-related sales.".

Once the Godzilla of personal computing, Intel haven't been having a brilliant few years. Back in 2024, they recorded a multi-billion dollar quarterly loss, pushing then-CEO Pat Gelsinger to resign. As regards sales of gaming PCs, they've fallen behind AMD, though they've reportedly taken some ground back recently as regards desktop CPUs. As regards graphics cards, they have long been dwarfed by Nvidia.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that rockstar Games has had an incredible week following the launch of GTA 6, but the same can't be remarked for the developers who were hoping to secure formal recognition for their union.
  • As VGC reports, the ballot had a high turnout among the roughly 1,600 eligible employees.
  • The ballot opened on November 12 and closed today, November 26.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that rockstar Games has had an incredible week following the launch of GTA 6, but the same can't be remarked for the developers who were hoping to secure formal recognition for their union. The results of a ballot among Rockstar's UK employees are out, and roughly three-quarters of those who voted have rejected the proposed agreement with the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB).

As VGC reports, the ballot had a high turnout among the roughly 1,600 eligible employees. Only 25% of votes were in favor of the deal. It's a disappointing outcome for the organizers, especially considering that they managed to get as far as negotiating an agreement with Rockstar after last year's controversial dismissals.

The ballot opened on November 12 and closed today, November 26. Had the vote gone the other way, Rockstar would have been home to the largest formally recognized union in the UK video game industry, according to the IWGB.

The negotiations weren't just about securing better salaries for GTA 6 developers. The proposed arrangement would have given staff a means of collectively negotiating everything from overtime compensation to pensions, as well as a say in how the firm handles redundancies and the use of AI.

Rockstar had already stated it would recognize the union if its staff wanted one. What makes today's outcome particularly striking is that the agreement didn't fall apart at the negotiating table. It was the vote among employees that ultimately put an end to it.

It was the vote among employees that ultimately put an end to it.

Sources indicate that speaking about the result, Rockstar's head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, remarked it demonstrated employees' preference for dealing directly with the company. The IWGB, meanwhile, acknowledged that it still needs to earn the confidence of more staff members.

That doesn't mean the Rockstar Game Workers Union has ceased to exist, nor does it mean that employees have lost their right to join it. The union can still represent its members, but Rockstar won't be bound by the formal bargaining arrangement that was put to a vote.

Recent findings suggest that it's worth remembering how unlikely it might have seemed a year ago that Rockstar's union organizers would even get to hold this vote. In October 2025, the company dismissed dozens of employees in an incident that subsequently led to an employment tribunal in the UK.

The IWGB alleged that the staff were targeted because of their involvement in union organizing. Rockstar, on the other hand, maintained that the dismissals were related to the sharing of confidential information on Discord. Today's ballot result doesn't settle that dispute, and the tribunal's outcome is still pending.

The timing of the vote also makes for a rather odd contrast with what's been happening outside Rockstar's offices. GTA 6 accounted for more than half of active PS5 and Xbox players tracked by Circana on launch day, and the game has already brought in billions of dollars in retail sales.

For some developers, though, the question is what happens to their jobs now that the game they've spent years working on is finally out. Even the commercial success of a game as substantial as GTA 6 can't guarantee that there won't be redundancies further down the line. That was one of the concerns the union wanted to address before the launch.

In a recent development, the IWGB says it intends to keep organizing at Rockstar despite the vote. Hundreds of employees backed recognition, so the organizers aren't starting from scratch. Convincing the rest of their colleagues, however, is going to be a considerably bigger task than getting Rockstar to agree to hold the ballot in the first place.

Breaking: Loneliness is making us sick, but we may be treating it all wrong

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (724 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that research has established that loneliness can have serious consequences for physical health.
  • Published in Social Problems, the study examines how chronic loneliness and social isolation became recognized as major public health concerns after researchers uncovered links to illness, premature death, and increased healthcare spending.
  • Previous studies highlighted in the research illustrate the severity of these consequences.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that research has established that loneliness can have serious consequences for physical health. However, a latest University of Michigan study warns that treating loneliness primarily as a health problem could shift responsibility away from society and place it on a healthcare system that lacks the tools to restore meaningful social connections.

Published in Social Problems, the study examines how chronic loneliness and social isolation became recognized as major public health concerns after researchers uncovered links to illness, premature death, and increased healthcare spending.

Previous studies highlighted in the research illustrate the severity of these consequences. One estimated that lacking social connections could be as harmful to health as smoking 15 cigarettes a day. Another found that loneliness, social isolation, and living alone were each associated with an approximately 30% higher risk of premature death. The financial burden is also substantial, with separate research estimating that social isolation costs Medicare $6.7 billion each year in care for older adults.

"Once people saw these findings, they began to treat loneliness as urgent," said University of Michigan doctoral student Sofia Hiltner. "But it made me wonder: Why do we only consider problems important once they are tied to health?".

The Problem With Medicalizing Loneliness.

To understand how loneliness became a medical concern, Hiltner conducted interviews with experts and reviewed more than a decade of media coverage, medical journal articles, and academic literature.

In a recent development, her analysis revealed that establishing a connection between loneliness and poor health helped the problem gain credibility. However, it also encouraged what she describes as a "logical leap": the belief that any problem affecting human health should become the responsibility of the healthcare system.

"Not everything that relates to health belongs in healthcare," she noted. "Doctors can screen patients and connect them to services, but they cannot rebuild communities or shorten work hours.".

Hiltner, a predoctoral trainee in social demography at the Population Studies Center within the University of Michigan's Institute for Social Research, was inspired to investigate loneliness after witnessing her grandmother become increasingly isolated as she aged.

When Hiltner entered graduate school to research social isolation among older adults, she learned that clinical trials were investigating a "loneliness pill." The discovery prompted her to question why loneliness was being approached primarily as a medical condition rather than a social problem.

Sources indicate that "After my grandfather died, my grandmother lived alone and there was little structure in her life," Hiltner mentioned. "She didn't seem to have many friends or activities. It made me think about everything that happened throughout her life that led to that point. I wondered about the social policies, in addition to dynamics at the family level, that could have helped prevent that situation.".

Finding Solutions Beyond the Healthcare System.

Interestingly, Hiltner found that the medical community was initially reluctant to take responsibility for addressing loneliness. Much of the momentum behind incorporating loneliness into healthcare instead came from academic researchers, government health officials, and insurance companies.

Although recognizing loneliness as a medical concern can generate greater awareness and encourage intervention, it may also divert valuable resources from efforts to address the social circumstances that leave people isolated.

In a recent development, "There is the risk that defining loneliness as medical crowds out other ways of responding to the issue," she said. "Attention, time and resources are limited. On the other hand, framing it as medical may inspire more action than would have otherwise happened.".

Hiltner hopes her findings will encourage policymakers to reconsider how they define social problems and explore preventive strategies that address their underlying causes before they develop into serious health concerns.

It has been revealed that "I would like them to reflect on the strengths and limitations of addressing problems through the healthcare system, and look farther upstream to understand how a problem emerges, considering ways to intervene before it occurs," she noted. "Healthcare can help, but it can only go so far.".

Materials provided by University of Michigan. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Tech Report: Each newly introduced GTA moves the series closer and closer to the original Mafia, the open-world game that bettered Rockstar

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (932 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that this week sees the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the open-world crime 'em up that's been in development for at least eight years and has been waited on by fans for even longer.
  • Released less than a year after Grand Theft Auto 3, Mafia is perhaps a more prescient example of Rockstar's future than their own.
  • Set in Lost Heaven, a shoe-in for 1930s Chicago, Illinois, you play through Tommy Angelo's rise from a taxi driver, who has a chance run in with the Salieri crime family, to one of the gang's main enforcers in their fight against their rivals, the Morellos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that this week sees the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the open-world crime 'em up that's been in development for at least eight years and has been waited on by fans for even longer. Naturally, over on PC we're still waiting for a port to be unveiled, let alone a release date to circle in our calendars. But, as happens whenever a latest GTA is on the horizon, I think about Mafia: City of Lost Heaven.

Released less than a year after Grand Theft Auto 3, Mafia is perhaps a more prescient example of Rockstar's future than their own.

Set in Lost Heaven, a shoe-in for 1930s Chicago, Illinois, you play through Tommy Angelo's rise from a taxi driver, who has a chance run in with the Salieri crime family, to one of the gang's main enforcers in their fight against their rivals, the Morellos.

In a recent development, the influences on developers Illusion Softworks are obviously cinematic, with whole sequences ripped from The Godfather films and Goodfellas (and I'd argue there's a sprinkling of Once Upon A Time In America for good measure). A habit they share with Rockstar, who also pull liberally from crime films that share the settings of their games. But Illusion Softworks are also clearly interested in capturing the history of the Prohibition era, too. The story begins in the aftermath of the 1929 Wall Street Crash and the depression that followed, running through until the late 30s, and you see that time pass in the city around you. Buildings that are under construction at the start of the game are completed by its end, a used car lot in Chinatown sits empty for most of the game until business picks up with the economy, but most enjoyable of all is that the cars driving the streets change. At first the roads are filled with Ford Model-T-inspired vehicles that basically look like horse carriages with engines, but by the end of the game they've all become much sleeker creatures that have left their early carriage influences behind.

The city Illusion Softworks built also has a dedication to verisimilitude that we see Rockstar adopting in their later games. As you drive Lost Heaven's streets, you must pay attention to speed limits and red lights, as speeding and running traffic lights will both earn you a fine if a policeman spots you. For fans of public transport, there are streetcars and overhead trams you can ride to navigate the city, too. Two other touches I love: when you reload your gun, you dump the whole clip instead of returning the unfired bullets to a magic ammo reservoir, and vehicles can run out of fuel if you drive them too far.

Recent findings suggest that much had been made of all the simulations running under the surface of Grand Theft Auto 6, such as fully realised cloud formation, a smell reaction system, and… fuel tanks that can run empty. No doubt they're significantly more impressive than what's on show in Mafia, and this isn't about putting the two games against each other (even if one of them was likely made for less than the other studio spent on coffee runs across its eight-year development). Nor is it about saying history recognised the wrong game: Grand Theft Auto 3 was a huge step forward in open-world gaming and Mafia was recognised and celebrated in its time. It's about something else.

In a recent development, back in 2002, Illusion Softworks offered a different kind of open-world crime game. One that was more mature despite having a lower age rating. Grand Theft Auto was undoubtedly more influential, sparking imitators that mostly opted to follow its tone and sensibilities – Saints Row began in a similar place to GTA 3 and as the series continued leaned further into the silliness and parody, for instance. But while for many years Mafia stood as a sign to an open world path that could have been taken, the longer Grand Theft Auto series has gone on, the more Rockstar have found their way toward the example set by Illusion Softworks. The games are still aiming for bombastic comedy at times, but they're also interested in the likes of newly-arrived-in-America Niko Belic, or Michael de Santa, a retired criminal haunted by his past. They're much richer protagonists than Claude, the silent character you play in GTA 3.

The Mafia series has continued, marked by ideas that remain as interesting as what was on show in the original. In Mafia 3, you play Lincoln Clay, a black soldier returned from the war in Vietnam and brought into the family. Set in a take on New Orleans, Louisiana, during the civil rights movement, you face overt racism. Linger too long in white, wealthy neighbourhoods and the residents will call on the police to move you along. And the Definitive Edition remake of the first game, released in 2020, is a rare example of a game that both captures the spirit of the original and justifies its existence by expanding and bettering the story. Though I don't think any of its sequels have been as innovative, nor as forward thinking, as the first game.

Recent findings suggest that I don't want to come across as Rockstar-bashing. The studio have continued to push the open-world genre forward with every release and I want to see what other developers lift from GTA 6 for their own games. But I'm even more pleased that as the studio's aged, their work has grown closer to Illusion Softworks'.

Breaking: My murderous wine merchant whines for a chance at republican rule in Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion, which isn't only about the money

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2090 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east.
  • Sources indicate that I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less.
  • It should, in theory, help that he’s my best mate, thanks to a well-timed feast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east. Yet, I still can’t reach out and grasp the throne that sits right in front of me. I’m Marco Sanudo, and the throne of the serene republic of Venice eludes me.

Sources indicate that I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less. I’ve managed to avoid punishment for that crime, despite the fact it earned me a fiefdom to rule while I’ve tried to up my patrician score enough to be the lucky party the next time a ruling Doge dies in office (or runs out their 10 year term). Sadly, Doge Leonardo, the mysterious masked lord who’s had an iron grip on power since the first couple of old blokes to hold the position in this playthrough popped their clogs, is proving incredibly tough to oust.

It should, in theory, help that he’s my best mate, thanks to a well-timed feast. It certainly did in being granted a pardon for offing that other Marco, but not even that and a plague which infected nearly everyone in the realm aside from me have paved the way to Dogedom. In the meantime, I’ve striven to gain wealth and influence. I’ve worked up to having four trade routes running at once, with goods like wine, iron, and textiles flowing from market to market across southern Europe and bringing a steady supply of coin back to my Venetian estate. I’ve built trade posts at the extremities of my routes, giving me the option of starting from further afield and reaching fresh lands if the cash flow dries up closer to home.

Industry observers note that this is where Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion has blended a bit with the game’s traditional feudal moneymaking to supercharge my coffers. The land holding I killed a dude for, the Proveditorate of Zara, means I’ve also had tax money from modern day Croatia to add to both my trade profits and the income my domicile generates on its own. I am, as the medieval kids say, minted.

Getting to the point of serious pocket clinkage is, as you might imagine given Silk and Silver’s focus on filling the game’s world with travelling merchant companies and wheeler-dealing republican patrician families, the beating heart of the expansion. A near-constant stream of notifications about prices of different goods I’m trying to hawk in different locations encourage me to regularly prune and re-work my routes so that max profits are being earned and no carrying capacity’s being wasted. The bubbling up of wars and plagues impacts prices in affected cities, making it a never-ending battle if you’re desperate to optimise everything within an inch of its life. I’ve found that degree of micromanagement unnecessary if the goal is just to keep a decent profit margin ticking over. Just remember to replace the trader assigned to a route if they die, recall them every few years so they don’t stress themselves to death, and check in every so often to re-evaluate whether you’re running goods that are suitably in demand.

If you stick at it for a decent amount of time, with a certain type of good - alcohol or jewellery, for example - your expertise in dealing in them increases, making it easier to sell for better prices. Trade routes left running between the same markets also gain boons from being in place for a long time, offering a counterpoint to rejigging them every five seconds to wring out a few more coins. Most of my routes have run along a path that includes stops at four markets, with the occasional location boasting a monopoly I’ve bargained for with the local ruler, so I don’t have to worry about competition at every stop.

It has been revealed that when you’re playing as a merchant who isn’t locked into the ruling inner circle of a republic, making your routes as lengthy as possible is one of the three moneymaking areas your company can specialise in. That first one’s caravaneering, and is the one I leant into in a non-Marco Sanudo playthrough. Beyond that, you can become an expert loan shark, lending cash to rulers or paying their ransoms in order to recoup interest and collect hooks you can use for favours. Manufacturing expensive artifacts that can be sold individually to collectors for a profit is the third option. The latter two I’ve only dabbled in a little bit as of writing, having earned enough gold mostly from caravanneering to buy the land containing the city with my home market and be anointed a Sheikh. So, beginning as a landless merchant is a nice alternative to Crusader Kings 3’s long-established wandering adventurer starting point, with both allowing you to work your way up from lowly serf to landed lordly dynasty in your location of choice.

In a recent development, if you’re after a more specific historical scenario, Silk and Silver has Guelphs and Ghibellines. This is where we find Marco Sanudo, as well as the other patrician family head I’ve played as thus far, Speronella Dalesmanni. The setup is that the Pope and the Holy Roman Emperor have had a bit of a tiff, essentially rooted in who should have certain powers, with different cities and powerful families in northern Italy taking either the Guelph (Pope-likers) or Ghibelline (Holy Roman Empire-enjoyers) side depending on what suits their goals or principles. I’ll be honest, aside from being another way to easily earn friends or enemies in the ruthless crucible of merchant republican politics, where votes and reputation-bolstering aid from other nobles are key, the situation’s not had a hugely obvious bearing on my playthroughs thus far.

Industry observers note that I think the closest it’s come is during my Dalesmanni run, if largely due to the existence of the By God Alone expansion allowing a new branch of Catholicism, dubbed Italian Christianity, to be created. The initial conversion push from the bishop responsible led a number of my fellow northern Italian nobles away from the Roman Rite headed by his Popeliness, making the Guelph/Ghibelline split more clearly defined.

Recent findings suggest that in the early hours of both my Sanudo and Dalesmanni playthroughs, I’ve been far more focused on simply trying to push the respective patrician families up the hill from posh toffs with naught but a vote and a manor to elected rulers of their great cities, with land holdings to match. Speronella’s situation in Padua is made incredibly tough by the fact she’s a woman in a world where every succession rule is designed to put blokes first, so I’ve had more success with Marco and his quest to become the Doge of Venice.

Sources indicate that as the head of a patrician family, one of select few elite clans who steer the oligarchical republic, I was faced with earning Marco enough respect among his fellow family heads that they’d consider voting him to the top of the succession list, thus securing his power whenever the current Doge got the boot. Pulling that off, while also not kowtowing to the requests and schemes of those same peers, isn’t easy. A large cocktail of factors go into determining whether another noble likes you enough to vote in support of your succession. There’s your patrician rating, which is upped by doing things which specifically show you to be good at this Italian noble house lark, such as establishing trade monopolies for the republic, gaining the Pope’s favour, or having close relatives who also hold key positions in the republic. However, how close a friendship you have with the target and how their character traits align with you also play a huge rule.

Recent findings suggest that thus it was that, at one point, Marco was best mates with the current Doge and had a decent patrician rating, but had only amassed 68 of the 72 points needed for noted Doge to vote for him because the Doge was generous, and therefore didn’t care for Marco’s ambitiousness. That same Doge either liked or respected Marco enough to grant him a council position and the status of regent, but he would not back Marco to replace him permanently for love nor money. This is the same man who liked Marco so much that when I pulled off that not-so-sneaky murder on another noble house head in order to inherit the keys to the Proveditorate of Zara, the Doge was instantly willing to pardon me and prevent Marco suffering any punishment for the crime.

Recent findings suggest that not even a couple of serious plagues hitting Venice, which at one point had all three people ahead of Marco in the queue suffering from smallpox, could get him on that throne. Eventually, it took a bit of lucky timing when his Doge mate died of old age - a few years after beating smallpox - to finally install Marco as Doge. Given that delayed promotion, as of writing I’ve not yet had enough time in the big chair to give a proper verdict on how it differs from regular feudal rulerdom in the long run.

What I can do instead is tell you a bit about the fun of council votes. The same pool of voters who in a republic like Venice, get a say in who succeeds the ruler, also vote on the passage of laws and decrees. One proposal you can put forward is a vote to change who exactly is allowed a seat in this voting pool. It defaults to just being heads of patrician families, but can be extended to include all vassals, or tightened up so only the Doge’s councillors or the ruler themselves have a say, that being the way despotism lies. As you can imagine, passing a change to who can vote can drastically change the state of play, either tightening up the number of folks who might oppose or support you, or bringing newly introduced folks into play in a fashion that dilutes individual power, but gives you more pieces on the board to mind or manipulate to your advantage.

I’ve found it suitably tough to orchestrate successful votes to change laws and customs which medieval Italian noble families, expectedly, have firmly entrenched stances on. Getting rid of checks and balances, such as the requirement to vote on banishments or wars - so the Doge can rule as a despot - has proven one such challenge, as has changing laws governing men being prioritised over women. I tried to pass equal succession as a substitute for men being put first while playing as Speronella, but met an insurmountable wall of resistance due to the region’s culture and faith. So, all I could do was try to put my young male heir in the best position possible to make the sorts of gains I couldn’t.

Recent findings suggest that much easier to weasel into place, either through some canny swaying or the offering of hooks, are laws giving state backing or other priority to trading in certain types of goods. Alcohol, for instance, which certainly hasn’t hurt the profits of Marco’s two wine trade routes.

Thus, cash continues to flow through the tentacles of my trade empire in sizable globs. As he’s now Doge, I’ve got Marco using the ample funds of Venice’s treasury to build a new piazza and have him focused on making the city’s already-strong trade league even more formidable, by attracting new members from the few other northern Italian blocs.

In a recent development, while I’m fairly sure there are folks who’ll find Silk and Silver's constant barrage of trade route notifications annoying, or that their power-grabbing skills and sheer multitude of money-making means combine to make playthroughs less challenging than they could be, so far I've found it another enjoyably sonorous string to Crusader Kings 3’s bow. Above all else, playing as a merchant gives more reason to invest in stewardship skills beyond just maximising your tax yields, while the republican politics of the DLC's main region fleshes out rewarding intrigue-focused builds. Diplomacy and martial skills are less key, but still have their place at times.

If you’re an absolute stickler for historical accuracy, you may well find other things to gripe about, but aside from the Guelph and Ghibelline conflict fading into the background, I’ve found plenty to like in my quest to become top Doge.

Latest Update: Common supplements rival antibiotics in treating severe gum disease

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1543 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A familiar dietary supplement combined with low-dose aspirin may offer an unexpected alternative to antibiotics for people with severe gum disease.
  • The findings, published in the Journal of Periodontology, come from researchers affiliated with Albert Einstein Israelite Hospital, Guarulhos University (UNG), the University of Taubaté (UNITAU), and the Ribeirão Preto School of Dentistry at USP (FORP-USP) in Brazil, as well as Harvard University in the United States.
  • The study suggests that combining omega-3 with low-dose acetylsalicylic acid (ASA), better known as aspirin, could reduce the need for antibiotics in certain patients.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A familiar dietary supplement combined with low-dose aspirin may offer an unexpected alternative to antibiotics for people with severe gum disease. In a year-long clinical trial, patients who received omega-3 and aspirin alongside conventional periodontal treatment experienced nearly identical clinical benefits to those who received antibiotics. Perhaps even more surprisingly, the improvements were still evident six months after supplementation ended.

The findings, published in the Journal of Periodontology, come from researchers affiliated with Albert Einstein Israelite Hospital, Guarulhos University (UNG), the University of Taubaté (UNITAU), and the Ribeirão Preto School of Dentistry at USP (FORP-USP) in Brazil, as well as Harvard University in the United States.

The study suggests that combining omega-3 with low-dose acetylsalicylic acid (ASA), better known as aspirin, could reduce the need for antibiotics in certain patients. The discovery is particularly timely given growing worldwide concerns about antibiotic resistance, which occurs when bacteria develop the ability to survive exposure to drugs designed to kill them.

Why Severe Gum Disease Is So Difficult To Treat.

It has been revealed that researchers monitored 109 patients with advanced periodontitis over 12 months. Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease that develops when bacteria accumulate below the gumline, triggering an immune response that can gradually damage the tissues and bone that hold teeth in place. Without proper treatment, the disease can cause teeth to loosen and eventually fall out.

As periodontitis progresses, spaces known as periodontal pockets form between the teeth and gums. These pockets can become increasingly deep, making it difficult to remove harmful bacteria through ordinary brushing and flossing.

"Patients with severe disease have very deep pockets, which act as reservoirs for bacteria associated with the disease. It's a very challenging condition to treat," says dental surgeon Nídia Cristina Castro dos Santos, the first author of the study and a professor and researcher at Einstein.

Putting Omega-3 and Aspirin to the Test.

Sources indicate that the researchers randomly divided the participants into four treatment groups. Every patient received subgingival instrumentation, commonly referred to as scaling. This standard periodontal treatment involves removing bacterial deposits and hardened plaque from tooth surfaces beneath the gums. Each group also received a different complementary treatment.

Patients in the control group received inactive substitutes for the antibiotics, omega-3, and aspirin, supplied in capsules that looked identical to those containing the active treatments.

A second group received metronidazole and amoxicillin three times daily for 14 days. This combination of antibiotics has some of the strongest scientific evidence supporting its use as an additional treatment for severe periodontitis.

Participants in the third group took three grams of omega-3 each day, together with a daily dose of low-dose aspirin, for six months. The fourth group received both interventions, taking antibiotics for two weeks while following the six-month omega-3 and aspirin regimen.

The researchers assessed the patients' progress at three, six, and 12 months.

Omega-3 and Aspirin Rival Antibiotics.

At the end of the study, approximately 58% of patients in the antibiotic group had reached the researchers' clinical treatment target, defined as having no more than four remaining deep periodontal pockets.

Recent findings suggest that the omega-3 and aspirin group achieved an almost identical success rate of 57.7%. By comparison, only 23.1% of patients who underwent scaling and received placebos reached the same target. Interestingly, administering both antibiotics and the omega-3 and aspirin regimen together did not produce any additional benefits.

Although antibiotics can improve treatment outcomes in patients with particularly severe gum disease, they are not routinely necessary for everyone with periodontitis.

"The use of antibiotics isn't considered the gold standard of treatment. Although metronidazole and amoxicillin yield good results in the most severe cases, their use should be evaluated on a case-by-case basis due to risks related to bacterial resistance and possible adverse effects," says Castro dos Santos.

Helping the Body Naturally Resolve Inflammation.

Recent findings suggest that the findings build on earlier research into the potential role of omega-3 fatty acids in protecting oral health. In a previous investigation, also supported by FAPESP and published in Scientific Reports, scientists found that omega-3 supplementation reduced periodontal inflammation and bone loss in rats. The protective effects were particularly notable when supplementation was combined with physical exercise.

Although results from animal studies do not necessarily translate directly to humans, the earlier findings provided clues that omega-3 might help regulate the inflammatory processes that contribute to gum disease.

According to recent reports, omega-3 fatty acids are a group of fats found in foods such as oily fish and are widely available as dietary supplements. Beyond their nutritional importance, they serve as building blocks for certain molecules that help regulate inflammation.

Castro explains that omega-3 works differently from conventional anti-inflammatory medications. Instead of simply interfering with pathways that promote inflammation, omega-3 helps the body produce molecules involved in bringing inflammation to a natural conclusion and supporting tissue repair.

This process, known as the resolution of inflammation, is an active biological mechanism that helps the body return to normal after an immune response. In chronic inflammatory diseases such as periodontitis, inflammation can persist and contribute to ongoing tissue damage.

According to recent reports, the researchers included low-dose aspirin because it can promote the formation of certain inflammation-resolving molecules. They suspected that combining aspirin with omega-3 could strengthen the body's ability to control the persistent inflammation associated with advanced gum disease.

Benefits That Lasted Beyond Treatment.

The researchers had originally expected antibiotics and the omega-3 regimen to work best when administered together. Instead, the findings revealed that targeting inflammation could produce clinical improvements comparable to those achieved through antibiotic treatment.

Industry observers note that "We imagined that the combination of antibiotics and omega-3 would be most effective in controlling periodontitis in these patients. We also believed that the results for the group that used omega-3 with ASA would be slightly lower than those for the antibiotic group. The result was surprising because the two therapies performed very similarly, paving the way for it to become a treatment option for these patients," says Castro.

In a recent development, equally intriguing was how long the improvements lasted. Six months after patients stopped taking omega-3 and aspirin, their clinical outcomes remained similar to those observed when the treatment ended.

According to Castro, this persistence raises the possibility that adjusting the body's inflammatory response could have lasting therapeutic effects. However, scientists are still working to understand the biological mechanisms responsible.

A Potential Alternative Amid Rising Antibiotic Resistance.

For dental surgeon Magda Feres, the study's lead author and a full professor at the Harvard School of Dental Medicine and the Graduate Program in Dentistry at UNG, targeting the body's inflammatory response could provide a valuable treatment option for certain patients.

"The combination of omega-3 and low-dose aspirin achieved clinical benefits comparable to those of the metronidazole and amoxicillin protocol, opening up a real alternative for those who can't take antibiotics, especially patients with allergies or intolerance to these medications," she indicates.

The potential to reduce antibiotic use has implications that extend well beyond dentistry. Antibiotic resistance ranks among the greatest threats to global public health, making it increasingly important to identify effective treatment strategies that do not depend on these medications.

"Demonstrating that it's possible to treat severe periodontitis by modulating the body's own response is new and relevant information that helps preserve antibiotics for when they are truly indispensable," states Feres.

More Research Is Needed Before Clinical Practice Changes.

Despite the encouraging findings, the researchers caution that the results are not sufficient to justify an immediate change in how dentists treat severe periodontitis. The participants did not have other significant systemic or oral diseases, meaning the results may not apply equally to patients with additional health conditions.

Larger studies involving more diverse populations will be needed to validate the findings and determine which patients are most likely to benefit from each treatment strategy.

Sources indicate that it is also important to recognize that omega-3 and aspirin were used alongside professional periodontal treatment, rather than as a substitute for it. Aspirin carries potential risks, including an increased risk of bleeding, and may not be appropriate for everyone.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Feres and her colleagues are investigating how the different treatments affect the communities of bacteria living inside periodontal pockets. Early microbiological findings point to a decline in bacterial species associated with periodontal disease and an increase in microorganisms linked to healthier gums.

These ongoing investigations could help explain why targeting inflammation produced such promising results and whether the approach can reliably benefit a broader range of patients.

"It's an vital step forward, but not the end of the story. Therefore, the message is one of cautious optimism: we have a promising, scientifically plausible alternative to antibiotics in select cases. Routine replacement will require more evidence," she concludes.

#144852. Tech Report: 10 Great Games That Defined The Nintendo Wii

Tech Report: 10 Great Games That Defined The Nintendo Wii

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1497 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 20 years ago, Nintendo launched one of their most ambitious consoles of all time with the motion control-focused and internet connected Nintendo Wii.
  • It has been revealed that designed to be the most accessible console ever made for its era, the Wii became one of Nintendo’s greatest success stories.
  • However, Nintendo’s resurgence and the Wii’s global popularity wouldn’t have occurred had it not been for the wide variety of exclusive games that introduced on the console and went on to define the Wii as well as Nintendo’s future prospects.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

20 years ago, Nintendo launched one of their most ambitious consoles of all time with the motion control-focused and internet connected Nintendo Wii.

It has been revealed that designed to be the most accessible console ever made for its era, the Wii became one of Nintendo’s greatest success stories. Its easy to understand controls created a phenomenon of people of all ages getting into console gaming for the first time, from children to senior citizens.

However, Nintendo’s resurgence and the Wii’s global popularity wouldn’t have occurred had it not been for the wide variety of exclusive games that introduced on the console and went on to define the Wii as well as Nintendo’s future prospects.

When people think of gaming rivalries, most people will think of the console wars between Nintendo and Sega in the 1980s and 1990s. While that conflict ended with the failure of the Sega Dreamcast, the two gaming brands’ mascots wouldn’t officially meet until 2007’s Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games.

Made to coincide with the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing, Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games was the first official crossover between the Super Mario and Sonic the Hedgehog franchises, with characters from both properties being able to compete in archery, fencing, rowing, and other Olympic events.

Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games not only represents the growing comradery between Nintendo and other video game publishers but also how much pure, simplistic fun can be had on the Wii by being able to play as some of gaming’s greatest icons in jovial sports competitions.

In a recent development, one of the best series of games to debut with the Wii was Shigeru Miyamoto's “Wii Project” which was a series of typically Mii-centric games tailored to showcase the Wii’s controls and accessibility to more casual gamers. One of the best of these games being Wii Play.

A Wii launch title for European and Asian markets, Wii Play was essentially a Mario Party-like compilation of minigames designed to highlight the versatility of the Wiimote in games such as the Duck Hunt-like Shooting Range, Billiards, Fishing, Find Mii, and more.

On a more personal note, my favorite of these minigames was the top-down Atari Combat-like Tanks! which has one or two players control tanks through toy block stages to destroy enemy tanks using the Wiimote’s D-pad.

In 2006, Nintendo revolutionized mobile 2D side-scrolling Super Mario games with the release of Upcoming Super Mario Bros. for the Nintendo DS. To capitalize on that game’s success, Nintendo decided to create a multiplayer, console-based sequel, in the form of 2009’s New Super Mario Bros. Wii.

The first newly introduced console-based 2D Mario game since 1995’s Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island, New Super Mario Bros. Wii was a near perfect translation of New Super Mario Bros. enhanced platforming gameplay to the Wii, with the added bonus of four-player local co-op featuring Mario, Luigi, Blue Toad, and Yellow Toad.

In a recent development, in fact, New Super Mario Bros. Wii might have been too perfect of a game, as Nintendo essentially kept on remastering it for years on end until the release of Super Mario Bros. Wonder. The former game was essentially ported to the Wii U and Nintendo Switch in the form of New Super Mario Bros. U, New Super Luigi U, and New Super Mario Bros. U Deluxe.

Many new exclusive games made their debut on the Wii, but arguably the most creative and cinematic of them was Monolith Soft’s third-person action role-playing game Xenoblade Chronicles.

A spinoff of the long-running Xeno series, Xenoblade Chronicles is set in a sci-fi fantasy world where life eventually evolved on two titanic robots, the Bionis and the Mechonis, that have laid dormant for millennia. The situation led to lifeforms from both robots fighting each other in perpetual wars.

While Xenoblade Chronicles may not have been the best looking RPG on the market in 2010, it more than made up for its blurry visuals with its enthralling narrative, centered around the orphaned hero Shulk and his mysterious Monado sword, as well as its more open-world structured gameplay.

Recent findings suggest that ever since Nintendo released the hit fighting game Super Smash Bros. Melee on the GameCube, expectations were high for its sequel. While many players would consider Super Smash Bros. Brawl to be a disappointing sequel, it still managed to delight series newcomers in many ways.

According to recent reports, like previous Super Smash Bros. titles, Super Smash Bros. Brawl is a crossover fighting game pitting Nintendo’s most famous characters against each other. Brawl innovated upon the series in many ways, such as featuring non-Nintendo characters like Sonic and Snake as well as featuring a stage builder.

According to recent reports, however, what really made Brawl an epic game in the eyes of many Wii fans was its cinematic campaign, The Subspace Emissary. It depicts many of gaming's most celebrated icons fighting and joining forces together to defeat the united destructive forces of Bowser, Ganondorf, Master Hand, and Tabuu.

It's rare for video game series to never have a bad entry, especially one as long as Mario Kart, but the hit racing series has consistently managed to release banger after banger. In 2008, the Mario Kart game everybody needed to have was Mario Kart Wii.

The follow-up to the hit Mario Kart DS, Mario Kart Wii was innovative for the series in many ways, as it featured 24 player characters including customized Miis, motorcycles, and was the first home console MK game to feature online multiplayer.

It has been revealed that what made Mario Kart Wii especially fun and the second best-selling Wii game was its Wii Wheel accessory. While it didn’t alter gameplay in any way, the Wii Wheel helped immerse players into the feeling of actually racing with friends online and in-person.

Recent findings suggest that in the same vein as Wii Play, Shigeru Miyamoto strove to expand upon his “Wii Project” in 2007 by creating a game that would encourage families to exercise. He more or less succeeded with Wii Fit.

Primarily played through the packed-in Wii Balance Board, Wii Fit is a fairly relaxing exercise video game centered around players practicing yoga poses, strength training, aerobics, and balance on the Board, with the game further tracking people’s weight and fitness progress.

Wii Fit certainly didn’t make anyone exceptionally strong, but it did motivate millions of people to become more invested in their overall health, and it did lead many friends and family to start exercising together consistently.

Sources indicate that while Wii Fit didn’t make most players work up a sweat, Ubisoft Paris’ music rhythm game Just Dance certainly did, and laid the groundwork for the Wii’s longest running support. Just Dance titles would release for the console well into the eighth and ninth console generations.

Initially a Wii exclusive series, Just Dance was an expansion upon dance pad games like Dance Dance Revolution, instead having players mirror the moves of on-screen dancers as best as possible with the Wiimote tracking players' motions.

While Just Dance 1 only had a modest tracklist of 33 songs that could be played across four similar modes, it laid the groundwork for a dancing video game phenomenon that’s still going strong today; one of Ubisoft and Nintendo’s most popular series among casual and hardcore gamers alike.

In a recent development, at Space World 2000, Nintendo publicly revealed the Super Mario 128 project as a GameCube tech demo, featuring 128 Marios running around a spherical surface. While much of this project would be utilized in Pikmin, it wasn’t fully realized until the release of 2007’s Super Mario Galaxy.

The third 3D Super Mario game, Super Mario Galaxy was one of the most ambitious entries in the franchise, as not only did it feature a more cinematic storyline centered around Rosalina and the star-like Lumas, but had players travel across the galaxy on spherical planetoids.

Recent findings suggest that this game design may have been nauseating for some players, but Super Mario Galaxy continued to show how the 3D Mario titles always strive to innovate upon each other to deliver creative, generation-defining experiences. The game even went on to directly inspire The Super Mario Galaxy Movie.

Without a doubt, the game that best defined the fun to be had on the Wii was arguably the greatest launch title of all time, Wii Sports.

The first entry in Shigeru Miyamoto's “Wii Project”, Wii Sports was a rather simplistic collection of sports games centered around customizable Miis playing tennis, baseball, bowling, golf, and boxing, in single-player or up to four-player local co-op.

However, Wii Sports’ simplistic design worked to its favor, as it allowed gamers of all ages and walks of life to easily play the game. The likes of Wii Sports bowling and tennis still being played by thousands of gamers worldwide 20 years later, in their original forms and within newly introduced titles in the series.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a significant component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

Industry observers note that the first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the new maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios says the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

The blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of substantial maps as Battlefield 6 at the moment is.

Another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

More Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off newly introduced gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

Industry observers note that battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios said we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

Ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

There’s even more exciting news for fans of big maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is currently in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

Sources indicate that for context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its issues elsewhere, and BF Studios states it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

Finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

Redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.
